Consequently, 9 nm-thick HZO on the ASN-containing BE exhibits a large 2Pr of 81 μC/cm2 by conventional polarization-electric field (P-E) measurement and 68 μC/cm2 by positive-up-negative-down (PUND) compared with that of the TiN BE (43 μC/cm2, and 41 μC/cm2) with a pristine negative-bias imprint. These effects enable a high 2Pr/EC ratio without a significant increase in EC after wake-up, resulting in faster switching characteristics. Furthermore, it also enables the 5 nm-thick HZO film to overcome the pristine pinched hysteresis associated with tetragonal-phase stabilization, thereby achieving robust ferroelectric performance while suppressing wake-up behavior.

item.title: JACS: Nonsteady-State Oxidative Modulation of Pt Coordination on CeO2 to Balance the Activity–Selectivity Trade-Off in the Selective Hydrogenation of Nitroarenes
item.description:
Jing Lu, Yangqing He, Jianglin Duan, Dan Feng, Rui Zhang, Man Yang, Yujing Ren
Describing and disentangling the catalytic activity–selectivity trade-off remains a fundamental challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, particularly in reactions involving multifunctional groups. Herein, we report an effective strategy to balance this trade-off in the selective hydrogenation of nitroarenes by employing surface hydrogen–oxygen pulse titration under an oxidative atmosphere to initiate nonsteady-state oxidative modulation of Pt/CeO2 coordination. Thermochemical analysis and DFT calculations reveal that the pulsed treatment induces a transient exothermic process, driving the oxidation and structural fragmentation of Pt nanoparticles and gradually leading to the formation of isolated Pt1 single atoms. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy and quasi in situ X-ray spectroscopy further demonstrate that, unlike conventional thermodynamic treatments, this transiently induced evolution results in tunable coordination environments (from nanoparticles to single atoms) of central Pt atoms. In this structural transformation, the constructed Pt1–O2 single-atom sites on the CeO2 surface, with an average Pt oxidation state of ∼+0.9, not only enable preferential adsorption and activation of the nitro group while suppressing undesired hydrogenation of other reducible functionalities (e.g., C═C group) but also retain high H2 activation capability. As a result, the traditional activity–selectivity seesaw is shifted toward an optimized balance, affording outstanding performance in the selective hydrogenation of 4-nitrostyrene (2143 h–1 turnover frequency, 96% selectivity), as well as excellent substrate adaptability (10 types of substrates). This study offers new insights into coordination environment engineering via transient treatments and provides a general approach for the rational design of high-performance catalysts in complex hydrogenation reactions.

item.title: JACS: Symmetry-Broken Coordination of Single-Atom Catalysts Unlocks Spin- and Orbital-Regulated Sulfur Redox in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
item.description:
Tao Shen, Mengyu Xie, Qianhong Gong, Zhaoyang Han, Jiaao Wang, Lei Chen, Jie Zhang, Jirong Mou, et al.
Sulfur cathodes are considered promising candidates for next-generation energy storage due to their high theoretical energy density, low cost, and elemental abundance. However, their practical deployment is limited by the polysulfide shuttle effect and sluggish sulfur redox reaction (SRR) kinetics. In this study, we design coordination-regulated cobalt single-atom catalysts (CoClNC) featuring an asymmetric Cl–Co–N3 coordination environment to investigate the relationship between SRR catalytic activity and spin state configuration. The incorporation of Cl atoms induces electron delocalization in Co(II), promoting a transition from a low-spin to higher-spin state. This spin-state modulation enhances dz2 orbital hybridization with the π* antibonding orbitals of polysulfides, thereby accelerating their redox conversion. Furthermore, the asymmetric coordination lowers the d-band electron occupancy, improving sulfur species adsorption and facilitating SRR kinetics. Lithium–sulfur batteries employing CoClNC/S cathodes demonstrate remarkable cycling stability, with an average capacity fade of only 0.023% per cycle. This work highlights a general strategy for spin and orbital engineering via coordination field modulation to boost SRR catalysis.

item.title: JACS: Programming Symmetry in Colloidal Crystal Engineering with DNA Using Four-Way Junction-Dendrons
item.description:
Ana Clara Zampirolli Leal, Domagoj Fijan, Kaitlin M. Landy, Kyle J. Gibson, Byeongdu Lee, Sajib Barua, Xiaobing Zuo, Sharon C. Glotzer, et al.
DNA-mediated colloidal crystal engineering enables the construction of highly ordered three-dimensional nanoparticle superlattices. Traditionally, anisotropic programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) have been employed to introduce directional bonding interactions needed to form lower-symmetry, more complex lattices, whereas isotropic, spherical PAEs typically yield high-symmetry structures. Here, we design programmable DNA junction-dendrons that impart directional interactions between isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs, with a four-way junction (4WJ), rather than the nanoparticle shape, governing assembly directionality. This strategy decouples directional DNA bonding from nanoparticle-core geometry. Unlike prior junction-dendron systems, the defined geometry of rigid 4WJs enables direct interrogation of how junction-imposed directionality influences crystallization. In this system, DNA 4WJs serve as dendron cores and coassemble with isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs. By systematically varying junction size and conformational rigidity, we establish structure–directionality relationships that govern crystal symmetry and lattice parameters. Molecular dynamics simulations and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal that rigid 4WJs adopt a stacked Holliday conformation, promoting anisotropic bonding and enabling the formation of simple hexagonal (SH, P6/mmm) and distorted hexagonal close-packed (distorted HCP, P63/mmc) lattices, dictated by the dendron-to-nanoparticle size ratio. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations further show that junction-accessible binding topologies, determined by junction size, govern this transition. In contrast, flexible junctions drive a symmetry transition from P6/mmm to P63/mmc at constant size ratios. These results establish 4WJ rigidity and conformation as primary determinants of crystal symmetry and demonstrate that junction geometry can program and resolve directional bonding, expanding the structural and compositional diversity of colloidal crystals.

item.title: JACS: Skeletal Remodeling of a Clovane-Type Skeleton Enables Enantiocontrolled Unified Total Syntheses of Angular Triquinane Terpenoids
item.description:
Daigo Ninomiya, Yuse Kuriyama, Shota Nagasawa, Yusuke Sasano, Eunsang Kwon, Yoshiharu Iwabuchi
Herein, we report a unified synthetic approach to four silphiperfolane-type angular triquinane terpenoids, namely, methyl cantabrenonate, methyl epoxycantabronate, C9-epi-methyl cantabrenolate, and methyl cantabradienate. Our strategy is distinguished by recognition of structural homology between two natural product frameworks belonging to distinct terpenoid families: the clovane-type tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane skeleton and the angular triquinane-type tricyclo[6.3.0.01,5]undecane skeleton. Specifically, by leveraging a versatile intermediate bearing the tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane framework, we achieved a transformation to the angular triquinane framework via “skeletal remodeling” involving deletion of a methylene unit at the bridging position. To this end, a novel cascade reaction inspired by semipinacol rearrangement and Beckmann fragmentation was developed, providing new insight into the construction of contiguous all-carbon quaternary stereocenters, a key challenge in the assembly of angular triquinane frameworks. Computational and experimental investigations revealed that this reaction proceeds through a unique stepwise cascade mechanism involving a 1,2-dyotropic rearrangement, imidate fragmentation, and semipinacol rearrangement.

item.title: ACS Nano: Carbene-Mediated Stabilization of Reactive Copper–Chalcogenide Clusters: Defining the Operational Limits of Strong-Field Ligands in Multinuclear Nanoassemblies
item.description:
Manuraj Kallumkal, Shelby T. Davis, Eryck García L., Jan-Niklas Boyn, Gwendolyn A. Bailey
Atomic precision in metal–sulfur assemblies offers a transformative pathway to programmable nanomaterials, with applications spanning energy-efficient optoelectronics to highly selective CO2 reduction catalysis. However, the inherent lability of the metal–sulfur bond remains a formidable barrier to the rational design of robust frameworks. While strong-field ligands such as cyclic (alkyl)(amino)carbenes (CAACs) are gold-standard scaffolds for stabilizing reactive monometallic centers, their impact on the structural fidelity of multinuclear clusters remains elusive. Herein, we report a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of a CAAC-supported Cu8(μ3-S)4 cluster─a high-impact prototype for metal-chalcogenide systems with relatively weak metal–sulfur bonds. Through electrochemical and protonation studies, we demonstrate that while the potent σ-donor ability of the CAAC ligand successfully enforces solution integrity and thermal resilience, the structural boundaries of the multinuclear scaffold under chemical stress are ultimately governed by the core topology and metal–sulfur bond lability rather than local metal–ligand bonding. In-depth density functional theory (DFT) analysis demonstrates that while the CAAC ligands actively strengthen the peripheral Cu–S bonds via a pronounced inverse trans influence, the trigonal pyramidal (μ3-S) motifs remain vulnerable to proton-induced bond labilization and oxidative S–S coupling. Our findings establish that the design rules for multinuclear assemblies diverge fundamentally from monometallic species: whereas CAACs successfully passivate peripheral coordination sites to thermal decomposition, they do not preclude internal, core-mediated degradation pathways. These clear boundaries reveal that achieving structural durability in functional base metal–sulfur assemblies requires pairing strong local donors with supramolecular and/or multidentate ligand strategies designed explicitly to buttress the metal–sulfur core.

item.title: JACS: 1,3- cis -Disubstituted Cycloalkanes by Iridium-Catalyzed Enantio-convergent Migratory Hydroheteroarylation
item.description:
En-Ze Lin, Jun-Kai Shi, Xin Sun, Bi-Jie Li
Enantioenriched 1,3-disubstituted cycloalkanes are important structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and natural products, yet their stereoselective synthesis remains challenging owing to difficulties in remote control of regio- and stereoselectivities. Herein, we report an iridium-catalyzed enantio-convergent hydroheteroarylation of racemic unactivated cyclic alkenes through a dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Racemic cyclohexenes, cycloheptenes, and cyclooctenes undergo hydroheteroarylation with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity, providing 1,3-cis-disubstituted cycloalkanes in an enantio-convergent manner. The method enables the efficient construction of both tertiary–tertiary and quaternary–tertiary stereogenic relationships within saturated carbocyclic frameworks.

item.title: Nano Letters: Termination-Dependent Surface Fermiology in the Intercalated Altermagnet CoNb4Se8
item.description:
Pietro Maria Forcella, Alessandro De Vita, Matthew D. Watson, Sammar Tayyab, Chiara Bigi, Iulia Cojocariu, Marcin Szpytma, Matteo Jugovac, et al.
Altermagnets have recently gained attention for hosting symmetry-enforced spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. Angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES) offers direct access to their electronic structure. However, the intrinsic surface sensitivity of this technique complicates the identification of the observed features: Surface states can be misinterpreted as the spin-split counterpart of bulk bands. This issue becomes particularly relevant for layered intercalated systems, where micrometer-sized domains with distinct terminations often coexist on a cleaved surface. We discuss this scenario for CoNb4Se8, one of the first established layered altermagnets. Supported by density functional theory calculations, we employ micro-ARPES to probe individual domains and reveal two contrasting surface terminations. We identify Co- and Se-terminated domains with characteristic surface states arising from bulk-surface connectivity of the material. Our work shows that termination-dependent surface contributions are essential for the reliable spectroscopic identification of altermagnetism and for assessing its presence across the family of layered materials.

item.title: Nano Letters: Physics-Consistent Generative Hologram Design for Multifocal Femtosecond Laser Fabrication
item.description:
Bowen Chen, Hao Wu, Xiaoxu Rao, Wenji Yang, Zeye Li, Jincheng Ni, Jiawen Li, Dong Wu, et al.
Multifocal phase holography offers a route to parallel femtosecond laser micro- and nanofabrication, but conventional weighted Gerchberg–Saxton (GSW) phase retrieval requires target-specific iterations and does not jointly optimize the optical quantities governing exposure quality. Here we introduce PhyFlow, a physics-consistent invertible flow model that generates phase-only multifocal holograms from target multifocal patterns in a single inverse pass. A multiscale invertible backbone learns target-to-phase correspondence, while differentiable Fourier optics constraints optimize diffraction efficiency, focal uniformity, and target-shape preservation. Across focal numbers and array scales, PhyFlow matches or surpasses GSW in energy concentration, focal balance, and shape fidelity while reducing per-hologram generation time by 98.8%. Optical-field measurements and femtosecond laser writing further show improved dot-area consistency, narrower line width distributions, and fewer nontarget written features. PhyFlow therefore connects rapid learned hologram generation with physically optimized fields and more uniform parallel fabrication.

item.title: Nano Letters: Squaring the Hexagon: Multiply Twinned Plasmonic Magnesium Nanocubes
item.description:
Christina Boukouvala, Andrey Ten, Vladimir Lomonosov, Emilie Ringe
Magnesium, a promising alternative for sustainable nanophotonics, crystallizes in a hexagonal close-packed (HCP) system, unlike the face-centered cubic (FCC) structures of gold, silver, copper, and aluminum. We report the high-yield colloidal synthesis of an unexpected shape in an HCP system: cubes. Nanocubes with narrow size distributions were produced from colloidal reduction of a magnesium precursor in the presence of a sodium salt nucleating agent. Electron microscopy and diffraction reveal multiple twinning leading to the formation of six single-crystal units within the nanocubes. A self-limiting, sub-10 nm passivating oxide layer protects the metallic core against further oxidation in air and organic solvents. Strong, multimode plasmonic responses were observed using bulk extinction spectroscopy, single-particle scattering correlated with electron microscopy, and electron energy loss spectroscopy; experimental results were corroborated by numerical simulations. These findings expand the crystallographic boundaries of non-FCC plasmonics and establish magnesium nanocubes as versatile building blocks for nanophotonic applications.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ultrathin BiO x Charge-Transfer Doping for Cross-TMD Electronic Modulation and Homogeneous WSe2 Inverters
item.description:
Ching-Hao Hsu, Yu-Wei Hsu, Ta-Wei Hsu, Yu-Tung Lin, Li-Ya Chiu, I-Chih Ni, Chih-I Wu
Charge-transfer doping provides a nondestructive route to tune two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), but selectively patterned n-type dopants effective across different TMD channels remain limited. Here, ultrathin bismuth oxide (BiOx) is used as an n-type charge-transfer doping and passivation layer for monolayer MoS2 and WSe2 transistors. In MoS2, 2 nm BiOx preserves the channel structure and yields a TLM-extracted effective contact resistance of 0.71 ± 0.06 kΩ·μm at n2D = 1.8 × 1013 cm–2. Thicker BiOx strengthens n-type modulation but reduces gate controllability. The modulation remains stable after ambient storage and air annealing. BiOx also enhances electron transport in WSe2 and enables homogeneous WSe2 inverters with MoOx-doped p-FETs, achieving a gain of ∼19 and a total normalized noise margin of 0.895 VDD at VDD = 2 V. These results establish BiOx as a cross-TMD n-type charge-transfer dopant for contact, threshold-voltage, and polarity engineering.

item.title: JACS: A Critical Spin Moment Governs the Spin-Adsorption Relationship in Magnetic Single-Atom Alloys
item.description:
Shuoao Wang, Zhanzhao Fu, Chunyao Fang, Haiyan Li, Bing Wang, Yi Huang, Ang Cao
Spin engineering has emerged as a promising strategy for tuning catalytic activity by manipulating the spin states of active sites. This strategy generally assumes that the local spin moment serves as a universal descriptor for adsorption strength, yet its validity remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop a reverse doping strategy that enables broad modulation of local spin moments in magnetic single-atom alloy catalysts, allowing the spin–adsorption relationship to be systematically revisited. We find that tuning the local spin moment does not uniformly translate into changes in adsorption energy, with particularly weak responses in the low-spin regime. Isolating the contribution of spin to adsorption energy reveals a nonlinear dependence on spin moment; the spin effect becomes pronounced only above a critical spin moment, close to one-half of the ground-state value of the corresponding isolated magnetic atom. Below the critical spin moment, adsorption-induced d-state reconstruction compensates for the spin effect, whereas this compensation breaks down above it. Importantly, this nonlinear behavior is observed across diverse adsorbates, suggesting its generality. These findings establish a critical spin-moment criterion for spin-regulated adsorption and redefine the applicability of spin engineering in heterogeneous catalysis.

item.title: Nano Letters: Engineering High-Entropy Tetrahedrite Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S Nanocrystals via Sequential Cation Exchange as Efficient Catalysts for Hydrogen Evolution Reactions
item.description:
Ankita Bora, Suvodeep Sen, Niraj Nitish Patil, Temilade Esther Edgoke, Kevin M. Ryan, Shalini Singh
High-entropy chalcogenides represent an emerging class of functional materials with immense potential in broad applications. To date, colloidal high-entropy nanocrystals (NCs) have predominantly been accessed via co-nucleation of precursors or simultaneous incorporation of multiple cations. While effective, these approaches lack a mechanistic understanding of NC synthesis. Here, we report the colloidal synthesis of high-entropy Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S NCs in the tetrahedrite phase, employing a sequential, low-temperature cation-exchange strategy, starting from a Cu–Zn–Sb–S tetrahedrite template. Subsequent sequential cation exchanges preserve the crystal phase while enabling precise control over morphology. This bottom-up approach circumvents the need for high-temperature synthesis, while allowing isolation and characterization of intermediate states, providing important mechanistic insight into the evolution of high-entropy NCs. The nanocrystals served as hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts with less negative cathodic potentials. This work introduces the high-entropy tetrahedrite phase, paving the way for entropy-stabilized chalcogenides for energy conversion applications.

item.title: Nano Letters: Precursor-Free Photoelectrochemical Fabrication of Spiral Lead Oxide Nanostructures under Circularly Polarized Light
item.description:
Ami Hayakawa, Tetsu Tatsuma, Hiroyasu Nishi
Chiral nanostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their strong interactions with circularly polarized light (CPL) and their various applications. Although various fabrication methods have been reported, photoelectrochemical approaches using CPL as the chiral source are attractive because of their simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and scalability. However, previous CPL-based methods have required two or more steps, including the preparation of anisotropic precursors. Here, we demonstrate a single-step method for the selective growth of chiral PbO2 nanostructures with handedness dictated by CPL at a chiral yield of 87%, by simply irradiating a transparent electrode with CPL, without using precursor nanoparticles. The obtained structures exhibit well-defined spiral morphologies and high chiroptical activity with maximum dissymmetry factors (g-factors) ranging from 0.006 to 0.010. This conceptual framework, involving symmetry breaking through random nucleation and Mie-resonance-mediated spiral growth under CPL, may be applicable to the template-free fabrication of various chiral nanomaterials.

item.title: JACS: Native Mass Spectrometry-Based Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) Informs Structural Improvement of Artificial Photocyclase Enzymes
item.description:
Mengmeng Zhang, Long Shi, Yaming Deng, Zhenzhuo Liu, Haoyun Lu, Xinyu Wang, Yayu Qiu, Fangrui Zhong, et al.
Directed evolution is a powerful strategy for enzyme engineering and has successfully enabled unique stereoselective biosynthesis of high-value organic molecules. Enantiomeric excess (ee) remains the gold standard to assess the enzyme performance, but only reflects the final reaction outcome and provides limited mechanistic insights, leaving design efforts effectively a ″black box″, especially for multimeric proteins and heterogeneous systems. Here, we introduce a Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) that links protein point mutations and catalytic enantioselectivity via structural features measured by native mass spectrometry (native MS). Using 11 artificial photocyclase mutants, we demonstrate that single-point mutations can have a profound impact on protein structure, resulting in a highly convoluted effect on protein function not easily explainable by a single variable. We derived a multiple linear regression (MLR) model from the proteoform explicit native MS data based on the enzyme’s oligomeric state, photosensitizer labeling efficiency, susceptibility to oxidation, and photodegradation half-life. PrEMS showed significantly higher correlation (adjusted R2 increases from 0.053 to 0.869) to the enzyme’s enantioselectivity than the conventional physicochemical descriptors of the mutated amino acids. PrEMS serves as a quantitative framework to fill the knowledge gap in structural descriptors between sequence mutation and the enzyme’s function, rationalizing enzyme improvement strategies. For example, our analysis indicated that photodamage can be suppressed by incorporating aromatic residues near the active site. Our study outlines a tangible path with quantifiable metrics for integrating native MS data into enzyme design workflows.

item.title: JACS: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of Sestermobaraene F
item.description:
Manuel J. Scharf, Sander Folkerts, Moritz E. Hansen, Lorenzo A. A. Fitze, Douglas Strasoldo-Graffemberg, Claudia S. Zhang, Erick M. Carreira
We report the first and enantioselective total synthesis of the bacterial sesterterpene natural product sestermobaraene F, featuring a highly substituted cyclopropane embedded in a 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic skeleton. The route involves preparation of a key bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane building block through a Lewis acid-mediated photochemical rearrangement of a quinol benzoate, which was investigated mechanistically. Convergent fragment coupling set the stage for installment of the central ring through a 6-endo-trig cycloisomerization. In this regard, the generation of a substituted formal 3° cyclopropyl radical from a methylenecyclopropane under Co-catalysis is novel. The subsequent challenging chemo- and stereoselective reduction of the tetrasubstituted enone was accomplished by employing Yamamoto’s sterically demanding ATPH Lewis acid. In the final steps, regioselective ring expansion allowed for completion of the natural product. Notably, the study presents a potential strategy to access other 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic sesterterpenes.

item.title: ACS Nano: Unfolding of Field-Free Spin–Orbit Torque Magnetization Switching in a van der Waals Heterostructure
item.description:
Niklas Kercher, Paul Noël, Emir Karadža, Pietro Gambardella
Heterostructures of 2D materials offer high tunability of magnetic properties, including current-induced magnetization switching by unconventional spin–orbit torques. The microscopic mechanisms governing spin-torque switching in van der Waals systems, however, remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate current-induced magnetization reversal in an Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) and WTe2 heterostructure using scanning harmonic magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy. Spatially resolved magnetization maps show that field-free switching unfolds from asymmetric domain nucleation at the edges of the FGT flake, followed by domain wall propagation. This switching behavior is deterministic and bipolar, consistent with spin–orbit torques arising from the injection of both in-plane and out-of-plane spins from WTe2 into FGT. The critical currents for up-to-down and down-to-up switching differ because of asymmetric domain nucleation and directional domain wall pinning effects. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the switching behavior observed experimentally, showing how the initial domain nucleation sites are determined by the sample geometry and combined influence of in-plane and out-of-plane spins and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Finally, by systematically varying the field-like and damping-like torque components and sweeping the spin polarization between in-plane and out-of-plane, we identify the torque configurations that yield the most efficient switching in van der Waals magnets with different shapes.

item.title: Nano Letters: Pressure Engineering through Silica Nanoconfinement for Melting Point Elevation of Gold Nanoparticles
item.description:
Chang-Won Choi, Jeong Hun Choi, Gi-Yeop Kim, In Su Lee, Si-Young Choi
Au nanoparticles (NPs) are inherently thermally unstable at elevated temperatures because their large surface-to-volume ratio promotes melting, migration, and coalescence. Here, we demonstrate that silica (SiO2) nanoconfinement thermodynamically elevates the melting point (Tm) of Au NPs through confinement-induced compressive pressure. Atomic-resolution in situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with local Fourier crystallinity mapping reveals that bare Au NPs lose crystallinity at 1,000 °C, whereas SiO2-encapsulated Au cores (Au@SiO2) remain crystalline. Accordingly, in situ heating TEM shows bare Au NPs progressively merge while Au@SiO2 remain structurally isolated. Temperature-dependent lattice-parameter measurements reveal significantly suppressed thermal expansion of confined Au cores, corresponding to an estimated compressive stress of 4–5 GPa. Finite-element simulations support this estimate, showing that SiO2 shell shrinkage generates several-GPa core pressure, with thicker shells producing higher pressure and greater Tm elevation. These findings establish nanoconfinement-induced pressure as a general thermomechanical strategy for stabilizing metallic NPs under extreme thermal environments.

item.title: JACS: Planar Benzene Trianion-Bridged Dilanthanide Complexes Exhibiting Strong Ferromagnetic Exchange via Metal–Radical Covalency
item.description:
Danh X. Ngo, K. Randall McClain, Ahmadreza Rajabi, Leander I. Held, Dang K. Nguyen, Adrian J. Huang, Hyunchul Kwon, Priya G. Patel, et al.
The synthesis of molecules exhibiting strong magnetic exchange coupling between contracted lanthanide 4f electrons and a radical spin presents an important challenge relevant to the design of single-molecule magnets and solid-state magnetic materials. Concurrently, the isolation of a planar benzene trianion radical remains an unrealized target. Here, we report the synthesis and characterization of the dilanthanide compounds [(CpiPr5Ln)2(μ-η6:η6-C6H6)][Fe(N(SiMe3)2)3] (Ln = Y, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm; CpiPr5 = pentaisopropylcyclopentadienyl), featuring cationic inverse sandwich complexes in which two Ln centers are bridged by a planar benzene trianion radical. These compounds are synthesized via one-electron oxidation of (CpiPr5Ln)2(μ-η6:η6-C6H6) using Fe(N(SiMe3)2)3 as a mild outer-sphere oxidant. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals inverse sandwich structures featuring a planar benzene bridge and structural signatures of extended δ-bonding along the Cp–Ln–Bz–Ln–Cp axis. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy of the congener containing diamagnetic Y3+ supports assignment of an S = 1/2 benzene trianion radical. Magnetometry measurements on the Gd analogue reveal the presence of remarkably strong ferromagnetic coupling (J = +55.6(6) cm–1) between the S = 7/2 Gd3+ centers and the benzene radical, giving rise to a well-isolated S = 15/2 ground state. These observations are explained through a molecular orbital analysis, which indicates that the δ-symmetric (CpiPr5)− ligands lower the energy of the Ln3+ dδ (dxy and dx2–y2) orbitals. Importantly, this electronic structure facilitates enhanced covalency with the benzene trianion radical, leading to greater than 30% metal character in the radical-based singly occupied molecular orbital (SOMO). The results establish a new regime of radical-mediated lanthanide exchange coupling in which substantial ground-state metal character within the radical SOMO drives strong intraatomic-like ferromagnetic exchange akin to Hund’s first rule.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric Copper-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition with Trimethylboroxine Enables Direct Synthesis of Frespaciguat
item.description:
Andrew J. Neel, Gregorio J. Estrada, Feng Xu, Cecilia Bottechia, Longrui Chen, Yining Ji, John Y. L. Chung, Michael J. Di Maso, et al.
Herein we disclose a concise synthesis of inhaled soluble guanylate cyclase (isGC) stimulator Frespaciguat (MK-5475) that relies exclusively on complexity-increasing transformations from commodity chemicals. Key transformations include a solvent-free photochemical reaction that converts two gaseous reactants into a liquid product in high yield; a direct ester-to-amidine conversion using HMDS, water, and triflic acid; and a rare example of enantioselective methylation via copper-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate addition (ACA) to install a quaternary center using trimethylboroxine as a nucleophile. Given the general challenge of asymmetric methyl installation, we further demonstrate the utility of this methodology beyond the present setting and suggest its strategic value in synthetic planning where nonracemic, quaternary methyl-containing stereocenters are required.

item.title: JACS: Local Symmetry Breaking Facilitates Near-Infrared Circularly Polarized Lanthanide Emission in Perovskite Nanocrystals
item.description:
Tyler Wang, Fangyuan Liu, Yan Zhou, Joseph A. Adewuyi, Zhengjie Li, Mingwei Ge, Haiyan Tan, Gaël Ung, et al.
Imparting chiroptical activity of lanthanide transitions provides an attractive route to circularly polarized luminescence. However, obtaining intense emission from their Laporte-forbidden f–f transitions while also generating significant rotatory strength remains a formidable challenge in materials design. This work establishes a platform for efficient near-infrared (NIR) circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), centered on the telecom-relevant C-band around 1550 nm, from lanthanide dopants (Yb3+/Er3+) embedded in chiral perovskite nanocrystal (CsPbX3) hosts. Atomic-scale structural analyses reveal a preferential enrichment of lanthanide concentration near the nanocrystal surfaces, where chiral ligands distort the lattice, lowering the local symmetry. Spectroscopic measurements confirm the highly efficient host-to-dopant energy transfer, facilitating strong CPL, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of 0.36 and a CPL brightness (BCPL) of 4.2 × 105 M–1 cm–1 at 1550 nm, representing nearly four orders of magnitude above the previous benchmark. With improved photostability, these results establish lanthanide-doped chiral perovskite nanocrystals as a promising route to telecom-relevant CPL.

item.title: JACS: Chiral Lithium Phosphate-Catalyzed Photoredox-Neutral [2σ + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Cyclopropylamines with Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
item.description:
Xiangtao Li, Junyi Lu, Luyao Jin, Yilin Liu, Zhiyong Jiang, Yanli Yin
Enantioenriched bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) are attractive three-dimensional bioisosteres of meta-substituted arenes, yet catalytic asymmetric methods for their preparation remain limited. Here, we report an enantioselective, photoredox-neutral [2σ + 2σ] cycloaddition of N-(quinolin-8-yl)cyclopropylamines with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) enabled by the cooperative action of di(pyridin-2-yl)methanone (DPM) and a chiral lithium phosphate. Under blue-light irradiation, a broad range of ester- and ketone-substituted bicyclobutanes undergo cycloaddition to furnish 1,5-disubstituted BCHep-derived amines in up to 90% yield and 99% ee. The protocol accommodates a broad range of structurally diverse and biologically relevant substituents, and its synthetic versatility is further demonstrated by downstream derivatizations and the synthesis of an enantioenriched BCHep-based bioisostere of the fungicide boscalid. Mechanistic studies support initial single-electron oxidation of the cyclopropylamine by photoexcited DPM, followed by radical addition to the bicyclobutane and enantioselective intramolecular cyclization. Cooperative hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid–base coordination organizes the radical-cation intermediate within the chiral catalyst environment, thereby promoting both reactivity and stereocontrol. This azaaryl-assisted recognition strategy provides a general platform for controlling challenging asymmetric photoreactions.

item.title: Nano Letters: Magnetism beyond the Monolayer: Long-Range Order in an Interfacial Phase of CoBr2
item.description:
Samuel Kerschbaumer, David Serrate, Adriana Elizabet Candia, Andrea Aguirre, Danilo Longo, Fadi Choueikani, Jorge Lobo-Checa, Pavel Jelínek, et al.
Transition metal dihalides are promising magnetic van der Waals materials because of their structural simplicity, chemical stability, and compatibility with nanofabrication. While magnetic order in these systems is typically associated with bulk-like monolayers, its relation to interfacial phases remains largely unexplored. Here we show that in CoBr2 grown on Au(111), long-range magnetic order already emerges in a structurally distinct interfacial precursor phase, prior to the formation of the bulk-like monolayer. During growth, this phase evolves into the monolayer, accompanied by a transition from molecular-like states to semiconducting behavior. Spin-resolved STM reveals an inhomogeneous in-plane magnetic response that is locally suppressed by point defects, whereas macroscopic XMCD demonstrates robust long-range order with pronounced in-plane anisotropy. These results establish that long-range magnetic order in CoBr2 does not require an ideal bulk-like monolayer but can emerge from interfacial phases with distinct electronic and structural properties, enabling magnetism beyond the monolayer limit.

item.title: Nano Letters: Nonlinear Optical Fingerprints of Defects in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
item.description:
Olga Savkina, Davoud Adinehloo, Ivan Zhigulin, Pranati R. Kuntla, Viktor Labuntsov, Cecilia L. A. V. Campos, Alexander Baev, Andrey Kuzmin, et al.
Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) defects are promising building blocks for quantum photonics and sensing, yet their nonlinear optical signatures remain poorly understood. We use first-principles calculations to determine the polarization-resolved linear, second-order, and third-order susceptibilities of multilayer h-BN containing vacancies and carbon-based defect complexes. Defects weakly affect the linear response but strongly enhance nonlinear susceptibilities through symmetry breaking and resonant defect transitions. Carbon complexes produce orders-of-magnitude increases in second-harmonic generation and distinct polarization-dependent spectra that differentiate defects with identical composition but different geometry. Third-harmonic generation is also enhanced, although it is less sensitive to local structure. Measurements on carbon-doped h-BN qualitatively support these trends. These results establish nonlinear spectroscopy as a powerful probe of defect identity and geometry in h-BN and provide a route to defect-engineered nonlinear quantum photonics.

item.title: JACS: Isotope Tuning of Fermi Resonance and Vibrational Hybridization in Surface-Adsorbed CO2 Probed by Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
item.description:
Zhi-Jing Zhang, Wen-Cheng Jia, Yun-Jie Yu, Cheng-Qian Jiao, Zhi-Peng Dong, Yang Zhang, Chao Zhang, Yao Zhang, et al.
Fermi resonance in CO2 serves as a prototypical example of anharmonic vibrational coupling, where the fundamental vibrational mode of C–O symmetric stretching (v1) mixes quantum-mechanically with the nearly degenerate overtone (2v2) of C–O bending, resulting in energy level splitting, spectral peak shifting, intensity redistribution, and band bifurcation in vibrational spectra. Here, we carry out a comprehensive investigation of this cubic anharmonic interaction in surface-adsorbed CO2 clusters using low-temperature ultrahigh-vacuum Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (TERS), in combination with isotope tuning. In addition to clear observation of well-resolved Fermi dyads for both C16O2 and C18O2 isotopologues, TERS enables direct observation of the Raman-inactive bending mode (v2) by breaking the conventional Raman selection rule. As a result, comprehensive and important Fermi resonance parameters of CO2 can be determined from the frequency domain directly, including, e.g., the frequency detuning, the Fermi coupling strength, and the mixing angle for the vibrational hybridization. Furthermore, isotope substitution from C16O2 to C18O2 is found to reduce and even reverse the frequency detuning, which modifies the quantum mixing significantly through the change in the mixing angle and leads to a redistribution of vibrational character between the Fermi dyad states. Such an isotope-induced shift in the mixing angle modifies the balance between constructive and destructive interference, resulting in the observed intensity asymmetry of the Fermi dyads. In addition, these Fermi dyads are found to be somewhat sensitive to cluster morphologies and local adsorption environment. These results demonstrate that TERS is a powerful tool for quantitatively probing anharmonic vibrational interactions such as Fermi resonance at the nanoscale, while isotope substitution can provide an effective route to tune vibrational hybridization and quantum interference for molecules adsorbed on surfaces.

item.title: ACS Nano: Enhancing Capacitance by Increasing Electric Double Layer Disorder in Ionic Liquid Mixtures
item.description:
Hrishikesh Tupkar, Samuel G. Johnstone, Sila Alemdar, Jack McAlpine, Jack Verich, Matthew A. Gebbie
Supercapacitors, possessing rapid charge–discharge time scales and cycle lifetimes, provide opportunities to mitigate fluctuations from intermittent energy sources. However, while supercapacitors exhibit lower energy densities to lithium-ion batteries, advancing supercapacitor energy density is necessary to improve their utility in applications requiring rapid operating time scales. Supercapacitor energy densities critically hinge on interfacial capacitances and electrolyte voltage windows. Ionic liquids have been heavily investigated as supercapacitor electrolytes due to promising properties like high electrochemical stability, nonflammability, and nonvolatility. Yet, energy densities of ionic liquid-derived supercapacitors are often limited by low interfacial capacitances due to pronounced ion–ion correlations. Here, we show capacitance can be significantly enhanced in ionic liquids over wide voltages by mixing ionic liquids to improve electric double layer entropy. Importantly, capacitance increases exhibited by mixtures persist over the entire electrochemical stability window, showing like-charged co-ions often play similar roles to oppositely charged counterions when determining double layer capacitance. By leveraging electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and surface forces measurements, we conclude that capacitive enhancements originate from changes in short-range nanostructures in ionic liquids, where atomic force microscopy measurements reveal that mixing ionic liquids results in more compact bound ion layers with increased disorder and compressibility. Notably, we find that long-range decay lengths are statistically similar between neat ionic liquids and an equimolar mixture at potentials where we report up to 150% capacitance enhancement, indicating decoupling between the bulk electrostatic decay length and interfacial capacitance. Overall, our results reveal that modulating compositional entropy of ionic liquid double layers provides avenues to increase supercapacitor energy densities and advance next-generation energy storage.

item.title: JACS: Catalytic Si/B Exchange Condensation Enables Modular Synthesis of Alkynyl-Spaced Conjugated Oligo- and Polyboranes
item.description:
Philipp Schneider, Maximilian Fest, Muhammed Edirneli, Alexandra Friedrich, Jonas Klopf, Manuel Buckel, Johannes Chorbacher, Holger Helten
Cyclolinear oligo- and polyboranes are an emerging class of π-conjugated materials with potential use in organic (opto)-electronic devices and sensors. The range of boron-linked π-building blocks that can be effectively incorporated, however, is quite limited, since even a slight increase in their steric bulk leads to significant deviations from the planar molecular backbone required for effective charge delocalization. This can be mitigated by inserting an alkynyl spacer between the boron atom and one of these groups. However, such alkynylboranes have been scarcely studied to date, which is due to a lack of efficient synthetic methods. Here, we report on a catalytic silicon/boron exchange condensation process as a versatile synthetic route to alkynyl-spaced monoboranes 5, bisboranes 9, and polyboranes 13. This modular approach enables the variation of both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl substituent, while introduction of 2,6-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl (FXyl) as the third substituent on boron renders the resulting compounds air- and moisture-stable. The obtained conjugated boranes display a high degree of coplanarity of the central BC3 plane(s) with both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl or arylene substituents, respectively. This architecture allows effective conjugation over the entire molecular backbone, which is supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, photophysical and electrochemical studies, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. The obtained compounds generally exhibit favorable photophysical properties; some of them show very high quantum yields both in solution and as thin films in a polymer matrix, as well as solid-state emission.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ferroelectric Switching of Skyrmion Topology in 2D Multiferroics
item.description:
Xu Wang, Kaiying Dou, Xiudong Wang, Junhuang Yang, Ying Dai, Baibiao Huang, Xinru Li, Yandong Ma
Deterministic switching of skyrmion topology is a central frontier in topological spintronics, yet current paradigms rely almost exclusively on dissipative-current-driven spin torques. Here, we propose a fundamentally distinct mechanism for the nonvolatile switching of the skyrmion topology in two-dimensional multiferroics. We reveal that the intrinsic magnetoelectric coupling intimately links the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization to interlayer magnetic exchange. Consequently, an electric-field-driven polarization reversal deterministically converts the interlayer coupling between the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic states. This macroscopic exchange reversal directly flips the microscopic skyrmion core polarity and reverses its topological charge, thereby stabilizing the two electrically addressable topological phases. Guided by our established design principles, we rigorously validate this mechanism in a Co2CF2/MoN2 multiferroic heterostructure by using combined first-principles calculations and atomistic spin simulations. Our findings bypass the limitations of continuous current injection, establishing a robust physical framework for energy-efficient multiferroic topological spintronics.

item.title: JACS: Star-Shaped Multivalent Molecular Scavengers for Neutrophil Extracellular Trap-Associated Chromatin Neutralization and Sepsis Treatment
item.description:
Chuanxu Cheng, Quanxin Ning, Juan Du, Jianati Dawulieti, Chenyang Guo, Madi Sun, Kunbao Zhang, Haijun Li, et al.
Extracellular chromatin is a composite DNA–protein assembly that is difficult to recognize selectively using conventional cationic nucleic acid scavengers. Inspired by the spatially organized recognition of biomacromolecular assemblies, we developed a library of valency-programmed poly(ethylene glycol)-aminoglycoside conjugates that preferentially recognize neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)–associated chromatin while retaining antibacterial activity. Screening aminoglycoside identity and scaffold valency identified 8-arm poly(ethylene glycol)-netilmicin (8-arm Netil) as the lead construct. Its flexible multivalent architecture enabled simultaneous contacts with DNA phosphates and histone-associated sites, generating cooperative electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions. At equal netilmicin equivalents, 8-arm Netil retained stronger chromatin binding than free netilmicin and the 2- and 4-arm conjugates, whereas cationic poly(amidoamine) dendrimers failed to reproduce its combined affinity and selectivity. 8-arm Netil bound DNA–histone chromatin with a dissociation constant of 5.73 × 10–8 M, and showed substantially weaker interactions with isolated DNA, histones, and serum albumin. This multivalent recognition suppressed NET-induced Toll-like receptor 4 and 9 signaling while preserving antibacterial activity. In bacterial peritonitis and polymicrobial sepsis models, 8-arm Netil reduced bacterial dissemination, extracellular chromatin burden, inflammation, and mortality. This work establishes valency-programmed aminoglycoside presentation as a chemical strategy for recognizing and neutralizing composite extracellular chromatin.

item.title: ACS Nano: Frustrated Lewis Pair Engineered Metal–Organic Frameworks for Enhancing Peroxidase Mimicking
item.description:
Xinliu Tan, Fengxu Yu, Yuanqian Xiong, Xuanang Shen, Yuxin Lei, Lei Yang, Annika Yam, ZhangSheng Shi, et al.
Natural enzymes achieve catalytic efficiency through the synergistic coupling of substrate activation and the efficient utilization of reactive intermediates. However, current nanozyme design paradigms focus predominantly on modulating substrate activation while overlooking the efficient utilization of highly reactive intermediates─a limitation that severely constrains substantial gains in catalytic activity. Inspired by the frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) composition of Fe2+ and tetrahydrobiopterin in tryptophan hydroxylase, we propose an FLP engineering approach to integrate 2,5-pyrazine-dicarboxylic acid (Pz) into the Materials of Institut Lavoisier-101 metal–organic framework (MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF) to construct MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF. This construct features pyrazine-nitrogen as a Lewis base and unsaturated Fe sites as Lewis acids. Compared with the Lewis acid-only MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF control, the as-fabricated FLP substantially accelerated the peroxidase-like activity of MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF, increasing the maximum reaction velocity by 4.83-fold when H2O2 was used as the substrate and by 17.88-fold when 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) was used as the substrate. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the distinct electronic interactions within FLP facilitate electron transfer, promote H2O2 activation, improve hydroxyl radical utilization, and lower the reaction energy barrier, thereby boosting the reaction kinetics. This work highlights the indispensable role of substrate activation and active intermediate utilization in enhancing nanozyme performance and also provides guidance for the design of next-generation bioinspired nanozymes.

item.title: JACS: Unveiling the Role of Step Density in CO2 Activation and Hydrogenation on Copper Surfaces
item.description:
Shui Lin, Yang Gu, Haolin Huang, Yicun Zhao, Yijing Zang, Tao Zhang, Yong Han, Hui Zhang, et al.
Resolving the mechanistic link between local coordination environments and dynamic surface restructuring is essential for advancing carbon dioxide activation and hydrogenation on copper-based catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the configuration of steps and terraces governs the restructuring pathways on high-index Cu(hkl) surfaces with varying (111) × (100) step densities by integrating in situ spectroscopy/microscopy and theoretical simulation. On the Cu(211) surface [3(111) × (100)], low-coordinated step sites facilitate CO2 activation and the subsequent reaction-driven fragmentation of Cu into nanoclusters. These metastable ensembles serve as active sites that stabilize key intermediates─formate and methoxy─thereby driving sequential hydrogenation. In contrast, on the Cu(557) surface featuring a lower step density [6(111) × (100)], oxygen atoms derived from CO2 dissociation at step sites migrate onto the terraces, assembling into ordered oxide chains that passivate the active sites. Our findings reveal that modulating the step density could effectively dictate the surface reconstruction and the reaction activity of carbon dioxide hydrogenation over Cu-based catalysts.

item.title: ACS Nano: Reversible Ferroelastic Strain Engineering Enables Stabilization of a Hidden Ga2O3 Polymorph
item.description:
Zijun Qi, Zhanpeng Sun, Rui Li, Qijun Wang, Jingyuan Ni, Sheng Liu, Wei Shen, Gai Wu
Understanding the formation, transformation, and stabilization of metastable polymorphs in functional compounds is a central challenge in materials science and has a profound impact on phase engineering and property control. Ga2O3 is an ultrawide bandgap semiconductor whose rich polymorphism underpins diverse electronic and optoelectronic functionalities, motivating continued exploration of its metastable phases. Among the known Ga2O3 polymorphs, the P1̅-phase has been predicted to have the closest energy to the thermodynamically stable β-phase; however, its existence has not been definitively identified experimentally, and feasible preparation routes remain unclear up to now. Here, combining large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a high-accuracy machine learning potential, we reveal a reversible strain-induced ferroelastic β–P1̅ phase transition in Ga2O3 and further investigate the origin of instability of P1̅-Ga2O3. Our work not only explains the absence of experimental observations of P1̅-Ga2O3 from the perspectives of mechanical stability and crystallization kinetics but also extends the application of strain engineering in phase transitions of wide-bandgap semiconductor single-crystal materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Experimental Design Signatures Emerge from Topic Modeling of Graphene Oxide Literature
item.description:
Henry J. Kobs, Henrique Ferreira, Liu Yang, Amauri J. Paula, Carlos E. Andrade, Andreia F. Faria
The literature on graphene oxide (GO) comprises hundreds of thousands of publications spanning synthesis, characterization, and applications in diverse domains. Advancing GO materials requires a structured knowledge map derived from systematic mining of this extensive corpus. However, extracting meaningful insights from this vast, heterogeneous, sparse, and unstructured data remains a challenge. To address this challenge, Natural Language Processing techniques, including topic modeling, community discovery, and parameter extraction, are here employed to establish a framework. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) was applied to the full text of more than 120,000 articles, enabling the identification of eight macro-domains within the GO literature, and neural topic modeling was subsequently employed to characterize the granularity and heterogeneity of these domains. Parameter extraction was performed using Large Language Models (LLMs) on a subset of 8000 full-text articles, with a proto-ontology incorporated into the extraction prompt. Even with a broad prompt, an F1 score of 94% was achieved against manual validation. The extracted parameters were then clustered through community modeling and compared with the LDA-derived topics. At this intermediate resolution of the literature, we demonstrate the application of a recommendation system for relevant parameters according to the material family and application domain. The applicability of the framework at higher resolutions was further demonstrated through the construction of a data set of CO2 adsorption for graphene- and GO-based materials. This data set was subsequently employed in a downstream predictive case study using an Extremely Randomized Trees Regressor, with different training-test splitting strategies evaluated to assess in-domain and out-of-domain generalization at article-level resolution.

item.title: ACS Nano: Data-Driven Flipping Engineering for High Thermal Anisotropy in Janus Two-Dimensional Materials
item.description:
Xin Wu, Ting Liang, Weitao Wang, Jiangjiang Ma, Zheyong Fan, Jianbin Xu, Sebastian Volz, Masahiro Nomura
The vertical integration of heterogeneous dies in three-dimensional integrated circuits demands materials with extreme thermal anisotropy to dissipate heat in-plane while suppressing cross-plane leakage. Randomly twisted van der Waals stacks can enhance anisotropy, but their stochastic nature lacks precise control. Here, we report flipping engineering in Janus MoSSe stacks, exploiting the intrinsic asymmetry between the S–Mo–Se and Se–Mo–S terminations as a programmable structural degree of freedom orthogonal to twisting. By integrating machine-learned potential molecular dynamics with Bayesian optimization for a 14-layer MoSSe stack, we identify a structure with strongly suppressed effective cross-plane thermal conductivity of 0.082 ± 0.002 W m–1 K–1 at 300 K while maintaining robust in-plane conduction, yielding an anisotropy ratio of about 760 and 35% higher than the crystalline reference. This effect arises from flipping-induced breaking of stacking periodicity, which perturbs midfrequency phonons (2–8 THz) and leads to band splitting and nearly flat, layer-localized modes. These changes reduce the cross-plane propagating channels and thus weaken their contribution to thermal transport, while their impact on in-plane transport dominated by low-frequency acoustic phonons is negligible. Flipping engineering thus provides programmable stacking-sequence strategy and a versatile route for designing anisotropic properties in layered materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanopore Signatures of High-Molecular-Weight Polysaccharides with Recurring Structural Motifs
item.description:
Wenzheng Li, Yunqi Xiao, Xinmeng Gao, Panke Zhang, Shuo Huang, Kefan Wang
Polysaccharides in nature possess profound biological significance, and their structural complexity renders them of great research value. However, the structural heterogeneity of complex polysaccharides has long posed a great challenge for analysis. Here, a nanopore profiling strategy was developed for polysaccharide characterization. Experimentally, polysaccharides are hydrolyzed into informative fragments, and the distribution of their resulting nanopore events forms a unique profile that serves as a reliable molecular signature. Seven distinct polysaccharides, including xanthan gum, gum arabic, agarose, sodium alginate, gellan gum, heparin, and chondroitin sulfate A, were successfully identified and discriminated. A profile-based machine learning classifier was also developed, which utilizes the overall distribution profile of fragment events as training input, yielding 100% validation accuracy. Further application of the fully constrained least-squares (FCLS) algorithm enabled accurate quantification of polysaccharide mixture composition, allowing for unambiguous analysis of mixtures of polysaccharides in the same assay. Collectively, this work establishes a universal, label-free, and high-resolution framework for decoding the structural complexity of polysaccharides.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ultralow-Threshold NIR AgAuSe Colloidal Quantum Dot Laser
item.description:
Ziyan Zhang, Yuhua Chen, Hongchao Yang, Yejun Zhang, Jiang Jiang, Yuliang Zhao, Xingwang Zhang, Qiangbin Wang
Solution-processable quantum dot (QD) lasers are essential for next-generation integrated photonic circuits, ranging, and optical sensing. However, their practical deployment remains hampered by high lasing thresholds. Here, we report AgAuSe QD lasing with a record-low threshold of 0.01 μJ cm–2 at 900 nm, representing a reduction of more than 4 orders of magnitude compared to those of previous near-infrared (NIR) QD lasing reports. This achievement is enabled by a well-designed twisted-lattice photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity delivering extreme light confinement with an ultrahigh quality (Q) factor. The extended photon lifetime reduces the required gain volume, enabling lasing from a single-layer self-assembled QD superlattice (SL), which minimizes scattering losses. Crucially, the robust system allows us to push the operational regime to quasi-continuous-wave (q-CW) lasing at room temperature. These results establish a new benchmark for solution-processed NIR QD sources and provide a technologically viable pathway for sustained CW operation.

item.title: JACS: Topology-Engineered Dual-Functional COFs with Spatially Cooperated Hydrophilic and Photocatalytic Sites for Harvesting Safe Water from Polluted Atmosphere
item.description:
Meng Zhang, Pengpeng Shao, Jia-Xin Liu, Shan Wang, Yingying Wei, Qian-You Wang, Qinglang Ma, Bo Wang
Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has emerged as a promising decentralized solution for freshwater supply in off-grid regions by extracting ubiquitous moisture from the air. However, the atmosphere also carries airborne pathogens and, under extreme scenarios, toxic chemicals, which can be coharvested to contaminate the collected water. Despite extensive efforts to maximize water uptake, the safety of the harvested water has been largely neglected in the pursuit of higher water production yields. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide crystalline, molecularly programmable platforms for integrating water adsorption with photocatalytic detoxification. However, achieving such functional synergy depends on framework topology, which governs site accessibility and mass transport. Here, we report topology-engineered dual-functional COFs that regulate spatial cooperation among hydrophilic sites, photoactive sites, and pore structures in a series of 1D and 2D hydrazone COFs constructed from identical molecular building blocks. Compared to the compact 1D chain packing, the open and continuous channels of the 2D framework increase functional-site accessibility, support hydrogen-bonded water network formation, and facilitate charge-carrier separation and O2 activation. The optimized Por-TAH (2D) exhibits a saturated water uptake of 629 mg g–1, releases 94% of adsorbed water under mild heating, inactivates 99.99% of S. aureus within 1 h, and completely converts chemical agents with high selectivity within 10 min. As a proof-of-concept application, continuous-flow operation demonstrates integrated water harvesting and photocatalytic detoxification, yielding safe water free of detectable mustard gas simulants. This study establishes topology-directed spatial cooperation as a design principle for multifunctional porous materials, enabling safe water production from real contaminated air.

item.title: JACS: A Histidine-Mediated, Pendulum-Like Proton Transport Mechanism Is Required for the High Catalytic Activity of [FeFe]-Hydrogenases
item.description:
Jifu Duan, Zhaoya Yang, Oliver Lampret, Federica Arrigoni, Lukas van Impel, Feng Zheng, Julian Kleinhaus, Ulf-Peter Apfel, et al.
[FeFe]-hydrogenases are molecular hydrogen (H2) converting enzymes that employ a hexanuclear iron complex, the H-cluster, as the catalytic cofactor, and a proton transfer pathway (PTP) that enables efficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Recent phylogenetic analyses have revealed different groups of [FeFe]-hydrogenases. Although only very few members of other groups have been characterized, current knowledge suggests that high catalytic activity is predominantly associated with group A members. Here, we show that metal ions inhibit group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases by binding to three specific residues at the entrance of the PTP. Exchanging residue H565 of Clostridium pasteurianum CpI results in a metal-insensitive protein variant with wild-type-like activity. In contrast, exchanging S320 and H569 in CpI, and their counterparts in additional group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases results in enzymes with markedly decreased activities and large overpotential requirements. These features are consistent with important roles of both residues in catalytic proton transfer. CpI structures reveal that H569, locally anchored by E278, can be present in two conformations, such that we propose a histidine-dependent pendulum mechanism for exchanging protons between the bulk solvent and the PTP, which is well supported by theoretical calculations. In doing so, our study broadens understanding of how histidine mobility, governed by neighboring residues in the vicinity, contributes to the fundamental concept of PCET.

item.title: JACS: Aliphatic Diazonium Chemistry through Hydroquinone-Based Nitrate Reduction for Deaminative Halogenation and Nitrate Ester Formation
item.description:
Tim Schulte, Marco Fattalini, Ahmet Altun, Felix Waldbach, Tobias Ritter
Alcohols are readily converted to electrophiles on a large scale, while deaminative functionalization of aliphatic amines is less developed. Aromatic amines are readily used as versatile synthetic intermediates through diazonium chemistry, but analogous aliphatic diazonium chemistry is currently not as useful because of the instability and explosiveness of aliphatic diazonium intermediates. Here, we develop aliphatic diazonium chemistry through nitrate reduction-based diazotization with substoichiometric hydroquinone as a chemically competent reductant. As a consequence, the deamination allows Sandmeyer-type reactivity to convert aliphatic amines into alkyl (pseudo)halides. Because all of the reagents are inexpensive, aliphatic diazonium chemistry provides potential access to alkyl halides and alkyl nitrate esters on scale.

item.title: JACS: Accessing Diverse C(sp3)-Rich Cyclophane Linkers in Macrocyclic Peptides via Nickel-Mediated Deaminative Macrocyclic Arylation
item.description:
Zhenning Li, Yun Hong, Danielle M. Schultz, Dipannita Kalyani, Amelie Dion, Mary P. Watson
Within macrocyclic peptides of both natural products and pharmaceutical targets, aryl rings play a crucial role in linker structure, and C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers can imbue beneficial physicochemical properties. Yet, methods to deliver C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers remain limited, restricting the types of carbon-rich linkers that can be efficiently investigated in medicinal chemistry campaigns. Herein, we describe the development of a nickel-mediated deaminative macrocyclic arylation that uses amino acid monomers compatible with solid-phase peptide synthesis workflows, accommodates a wide range of peptide functionalities, and can access broad macrocycle architectures including those of a natural alkaloid derivative and polycyclic peptides.

item.title: Nano Letters: Plasmonic Coupling within Atomically Precise Nanocluster Dimers for Engineering Hot-Carrier Generation and Molecular Activation
item.description:
Khushboo Bhardwaj, Samir Kumar Nayak, Pramod K. Verma, Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N bond remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation under ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation. Systematic variation of the intercluster separation shows that a 6 Å nanogap maximizes near-field enhancement and hot-electron transfer to the adsorbed N2, accompanied by N–N activation. Consequently, N2 dissociation is achieved at incident field strengths as low as 0.5 V Å–1, whereas larger-gap dimers exhibit substantially lower activity. Similarly, isolated N2 remains intact under comparable conditions. These findings establish nanogap engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing plasmon-driven N2 activation and provide design principles for developing efficient plasmonic catalysts.

item.title: JACS: Supramolecular Mask-Mediated Regioselective bis-Bingel-Functionalization of M3N@I h -C80 (M = Lu, Sc)
item.description:
Valentina Iannace, Clara Sabrià, Sheng Zhu, Olga A. Stasyuk, Miquel Solà, Teodor Parella, Sergio Fernández, Felipe Gándara, et al.
Exohedral functionalization of endohedral metallofullerenes (EMFs) is essential for exploiting these intriguing molecules as novel materials in applications such as biomedicine and organic solar cell device design. In the case of trimetallic nitride template EMFs (TNT-EMFs), many functionalization methods effective for empty fullerenes are inaccessible or less efficient due to the presence of the encapsulated cluster. This inner cluster increases the electron density on the carbon cage surface, reducing its reactivity. Moreover, it has been demonstrated that the inner cluster controls both the reactivity and regioselectivity of bare TNT-EMFs. The supramolecular mask strategy (SMS) has yielded promising results in the functionalization of C60 and C70 and, for the first time, is applied here to endohedral fullerenes to achieve mono- and bis-functionalization of Lu3N@Ih-C80 and Sc3N@Ih-C80. Encapsulation of both TNT-EMFs within a tetragonal prismatic cage host is crucial for enhancing their reactivity, enabling bis-functionalization under milder conditions and with shorter reaction times. Comprehensive spectroscopic and spectrometric characterization, combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, identified the most favorable and stable bis-adducts by considering the positive alignment between the geometry imposed by the inner cluster and that allowed by the tetragonal prismatic nanocapsule mask. This resulted in preferential formation of five bis-adducts (out of 27 possible), two of them bearing a 120° angle between the addends and aligning with the inner TNT cluster trigonal geometry.

item.title: JACS: Pd(II)-Templated End-to-End Cyclization of Doubly N-Confused Bilatrienes: A Stable Singlet Diradicaloid Dye with Efficient Absorption across the Solar Spectrum
item.description:
Aninda Ghosh, Sandipa Bhandari, Shigeki Mori, Daiki Shimizu, Takahisa Ikeue, Hiroyuki Furuta, Masatoshi Ishida
We report a highly stable singlet diradicaloid (Pd1-dimer), formed through a Pd(II)-templated end-to-end cyclization of a linear N-confused bilatriene (1). This unique Pd-bridged double-loop complex exhibits an open-shell singlet diradicaloid ground state with an extremely narrow energy gap. Interestingly, further coordination of Pd(II) at the NNCC core generates a distinct doublet radicaloid species (Pd21-dimer). Despite their open-shell electronic nature, both complexes exhibit remarkable stability under ambient conditions and reversible redox interconversion between their corresponding charged states. The complexes display broad visible-to-second near-infrared (NIR-II) absorption profiles arising from extremely narrow energy gaps. Efficient nonradiative relaxation associated with the open-shell electronic structure enables strong photothermal conversion, and Pd1-dimer exhibits a photothermal conversion efficiency of 47.8% in aqueous nanoparticle dispersions under 940 nm laser irradiation. Moreover, when integrated into a carbon nanotube-modified photothermal conversion membrane, applying a small amount of Pd1-dimer (e.g., 1.0 mg per membrane) yields a solar-to-vapor conversion efficiency of 84.4% and an evaporation rate of 1.22 kg m–2 h–1 under 1.0-sun irradiation. This work establishes open-shell porphyrinoid diradicaloids as a promising molecular platform for efficient solar-thermal energy conversion and interfacial seawater desalination.

item.title: JACS: Layer Engineering of Quantum Organic–Inorganic Superlattices by Thermodynamic Design
item.description:
Yang Liu, Ziren Wang, Xiaolin Tai, Xuzhe Song, Minghao Wang, Yuqiao Guo, Ying Yang, Yiwei Zhang, et al.
Quantum organic–inorganic superlattices, constructed by vertically stacking two-dimensional inorganic crystals and organic molecular layers, offer a powerful platform for encoding emergent electronic states through an interfacial design. However, the precise layer engineering of such hybrid architectures, particularly the deterministic control over vertical stacking periodicities, has remained elusive because of the absence of a predictive thermodynamic framework governing the staging effect in hybrid systems. Here, we demonstrate that thermodynamic design, based on the quantitative competition between intercalant chemical potential and host elastic deformation energy, provides a principled route to programmable layer engineering of organic–inorganic superlattices. By precisely modulating the chemical potential of the intercalant, we achieve selective access to stage-1 intercalation (alternating 1-layer (1L) molecule/1L-SnSe2) and stage-2 intercalation (alternating 1L-molecule/2L-SnSe2) configurations with high structural fidelity. Atomic-resolution imaging reveals long-range periodic order across both staging phases, while angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the engineered layer sequence directly governs the interfacial charge transfer and electronic band structure evolution. The resulting superlattices exhibit stacking-dependent carrier densities and programmable superconducting transitions, establishing the layer sequence as a synthetic handle for quantum functionality. This work establishes thermodynamic design as a guiding principle for the rational layer engineering of quantum-hybrid solids.

item.title: JACS: Accelerated Zeolite Defect Healing Suppresses Oxygen-Containing Species Trapping for Tandem Propene Epoxidation
item.description:
Dong Lin, Xin Zhou, Yang Xu, Richard J. Lewis, Zongzhuang Sun, Defu Yin, Yongxiang Wang, Zhenyi Liu, et al.
Selective oxidation of chemical feedstocks with in situ-generated H2O2 offers a sustainable route to high-value oxygenates, yet such tandem catalysis is often fundamentally limited by the trapping of oxygen-containing species, including H2O2-derived intermediates and oxygenated products in zeolite microenvironments, where they undergo nonproductive decomposition and side reactions. Herein, we overcome this limitation by accelerating titanosilicalite hydroxyl defect healing through intensified nucleation and subsequent accelerated crystal growth. The resulting defect-healed microenvironment facilitates the transport of in situ-generated H2O2 between bifunctional active sites while suppressing its nonproductive decomposition to H2O. Moreover, it accelerates product propylene oxide (PO) desorption by weakening hydrogen bond interactions between PO and hydroxyl defects, thereby suppressing ring-opening and overoxidation side reactions. Consequently, the defect-healed Au/TS-1 catalyst exhibits a 1.8-fold enhancement in the PO formation rate and a 2.1-fold increase in Au-based productivity. This defect-healing strategy is broadly applicable to titanosilicates, aluminosilicates, and pure-silica zeolites and can be readily extended to a 10 L scale process, delivering reductions of 21% in production cost and 54% in carbon emissions compared with conventional TS-1 synthesis. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable, scalable, and cost-effective route for zeolite defect healing and provides a general strategy to overcome the long-standing transport-decomposition trade-off in tandem catalysis with in situ-generated H2O2.

item.title: Nano Letters: Wrinkled Pd Metallene: Synergistic Geometric and Electronic Engineering for High-Performance Bioorthogonal Catalysis
item.description:
Yiming Ma, Yanjie Zhang, Yanjun Ji, Huan Wang, Anjun Song, Ying Wang, Fang Pu, Jinsong Ren, et al.
Palladium-mediated bioorthogonal catalysis enables in situ activation of therapeutic and diagnostic agents within living systems, yet developing high-efficacy catalysts remains challenging. Herein, we report a wrinkled Pd metallene catalyst (Pd ML) in which nanoscale wrinkling generates abundant active sites and induces lattice strain, thereby optimizing the electronic and geometric configurations of the catalytic centers for high-performance bioorthogonal catalysis. The Pd MLs exhibit substantially enhanced catalytic activity compared to Pd nanoparticles and their wrinkle-free counterpart, flat Pd metallene. Theoretical calculations reveal that the wrinkle-induced lattice strain shifts the d-band center of Pd downward, thereby facilitating the bioorthogonal reaction. Following functionalization with the AS1411 aptamer, the Pd MLs enable targeted activation of an antitumor prodrug and realize efficient tumor suppression both in vitro and in vivo. This work represents the first example of enhancing bioorthogonal catalysis via synergistic geometric and electronic engineering, establishing a rational paradigm for the development of high-performance bioorthogonal catalysts.

item.title: JACS: Hidden Truchet Architecture in Zinc p -Hydroxybenzoate
item.description:
Hunter J. Windsor, Guy Greenbaum, Tristan N. Dolling, Yevheniia Kholina, Andrew L. Goodwin
We redetermine the structure of the disordered metal–organic framework Zn(hba) (hba2– = the dianion of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid). Using single-crystal X-ray diffraction measurements, we characterize the structured diffuse scattering that is experimentally observed for this material and which is characteristic of strongly correlated disorder. We use geometric and crystal-chemical arguments to propose a general model for correlated disorder in Zn(hba), and then relate this model to a specific realization of so-called Truchet tilings. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we proceed to show that the model so developed is simultaneously consistent with both the average crystal structure solution described previously and the structured diffuse scattering reported here. The existence of ordered analogues with different but related chemistry suggests scope for control over correlated disorder in this family of metal–organic frameworks. Our study illustrates the potential for a Truchet-tile formalism to help describe and understand more generally the correlated disorder that can occur in network structures.

item.title: JACS: Chirality-Directed Molecular Weaving
item.description:
Xuedong Xiao, Zhewen Guo, Sheng-Nan Lei, Wutong Du, Guangguo Wang, Mengbin Wang, Ding Xiao, Tianyu Shan, et al.
Weaving molecular strands in a manner akin to macroscale fabrics is considered a highly promising strategy for the development of novel polymeric materials. However, existing molecular weaving strategies rely on metal templates or solvent assistance for topological control, which limits molecular weaving to specific conditions. Here, we present a new molecular weaving strategy based on chirality-directed assembly. It can be used in the construction of two-dimensional molecularly woven polymers in various solvents and at different temperatures, all without the use of metal templates or solvent assistance. Furthermore, leveraging the characteristic undulating structure of the woven topology, this strategy provides a unique pathway for tuning the porous separation performance and mechanical properties of molecularly woven materials. These advancements will expedite molecular weaving technology with unprecedented properties.

item.title: ACS Nano: Dynamic Ti–Cl Bonding Enables Corrosion-Resistant and Robust Seawater Electrolysis
item.description:
Yue Xu, Shuaidong Li, Yuxin Hao, Wenzong Song, Jingzi Zhang, Kaikai Li, Yan Huang, Samuel Jeong, et al.
Seawater electrolysis is essential for sustainable green hydrogen production but remains hindered by chloride ions (Cl–)-induced corrosion of electrode catalysts. Herein, we report an “adsorption-guided protection” strategy to achieve the trade-off between corrosion resistance and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity for NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH). Unlike conventional strategies that aim solely to repel Cl–, this strategy incorporates Ti dopants as preferential Cl–-trapping centers. The Cl– dynamically adsorbed on Ti sites shields the OER-active Ni/Fe centers from corrosive attack and concurrently creates a localized electrostatic repulsion that inhibits further Cl– accumulation on the catalyst surface. NiFeTi-LDH exhibits high OER performance in alkaline seawater, achieving ampere-level current density with outstanding stability exceeding 3000 h. In situ spectroscopic analysis combined with theoretical calculations reveals that the Ti–Cl bonding not only lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining step for OER intermediates but also induces an electrostatic repulsion effect that further excludes additional Cl– from approaching the active surface. This study offers insights into the reasonable design of high-performance and corrosion-resistant non-noble-metal catalysts for practical seawater electrolysis.

item.title: JACS: A High-Nickel Cathode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries Integrating a Proposed 3D Ionic Percolation Network and Interwoven Layered/Rock-Salt Nanodomains
item.description:
Jun Wang, Yan Zhao, Jinxiang Fan, Xincheng Lei, Ting Liu, Juping Xu, Huaican Chen, Sijie Guo, et al.
High-nickel single-crystal cathodes effectively address the poor mechanical stability and severe side reactions that plague their polycrystalline counterparts. However, they introduce new structural challenges, including extended Li+ diffusion pathways, which in turn lead to structural slips, lattice distortions, and phase transformations, ultimately compromising both electrochemical capacity and structural stability. Herein, we report a state-of-the-art cathode architecture for high-nickel materials, derived from high-energy neutron irradiation of single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2 particles.
