We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. We established a scenario for the large subunit biogenesis via macromolecular colocalization that may aid in the identification and characterization of additional genes required for achieving complete functional ribosome self-regeneration in a minimal system.

item.title: JACS: High-Resolution X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy of Soluble Methane Monooxygenase: Room Temperature and Cryogenic Insights into Active Site Electronic Structure Modulation
item.description:
Olivia McCubbin Stepanic, Sinjini Bhattacharjee, Christopher J. Pollock, Kara A. Zielinski, Rahul Banerjee, Derek B. Rice, Kushal Sengupta, John D. Lipscomb, et al.
Room temperature HERFD XAS (High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy) data collected on the stable Fe(III)Fe(III) (ox) and Fe(II)Fe(II) (red) states of the soluble methane monooxygenase hydroxylase (sMMOH) from Methylosinus trichosporium (Mt) OB3b using laminar flow cells reveal structural differences with varied temperature, pH, and presence of regulatory protein MMOB. High quality room-temperature data on the X-ray radiation sensitive MMOH-ox:MMOB state shows two distinct radiative reduction events, confirming the presence of a so-called semimet (Fe(II)Fe(III)) state in Mt sMMO, and for the first time presents the undamaged HERFD XAS spectra of MMOH-ox and MMOH-ox:MMOB. Clear differences in the whiteline and pre-edge of MMOH-red:MMOB appear between room temperature and cryogenic data, indicating the presence of cryogenic artifacts. In light of this new room temperature data, TD-DFT calculations based on optimized QM/MM models have been used to assign the structures of MMOH-red and ox states. MMOH-red and MMOH-red:MMOB have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate on the basis of pre-edge intensities, with minor perturbations in the ligand field seen upon MMOB binding. MMOH-ox:MMOB and MMOH-ox have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate with different protonation states at pH 7 on the basis of calculated models and changes in the experimental pre-edge energies and intensities for MMOH-ox:MMOB at pH 7.5. Together these results establish a revised structural and mechanistic framework for sMMO and demonstrate the potential of microfluidic HERFD XAS for capturing authentic enzymatic states.

item.title: JACS: Functionalized Olefin-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Mercury Capture and Recovery from Vinyl Chloride-Rich Gas Streams
item.description:
Mingming Wang, Haomiao Xu, Yurui Fan, Chaobin Shi, Jun Lei, Jiawei Lai, Weiwei Li, Qinyuan Hong, et al.
The calcium carbide-derived acetylene hydrochlorination route for vinyl chloride monomer (VCM, C2H3Cl) production remains a major source of mercury consumption and emission owing to its reliance on HgCl2/activated carbon catalysts. Selective removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) from crude VCM streams is intrinsically challenging because Hg0 must be captured from C2H3Cl-rich and HCl-containing atmospheres without coadsorbing valuable C2H3Cl. Here, we report a pore-engineered covalent organic framework (COF) platform in which olefin-linked sp2-carbon-conjugated frameworks suppress nonspecific C2H3Cl adsorption, while Cu-coordinated 2-(methylthio)ethoxy side chains create well-defined Cu–O2S2 pockets for selective Hg0 capture. These structural features afford an ideal adsorbed solution theory-predicted Hg0/C2H3Cl selectivity exceeding 20,000. Notably, dynamic breakthrough experiments under simulated industrial conditions containing 5 vol % HCl further revealed a Hg0 breakthrough time of over 10,000 min g–1 in C2H3Cl-rich streams, with a separation factor of approximately 52, demonstrating exceptional resistance to acid-induced deactivation. Treatment of the spent adsorbent with Na2S solution enables regeneration over 30 consecutive cycles and converts captured mercury into chemically stable HgS. This work establishes a molecularly precise removal–recovery platform for elemental mercury from chemically complex industrial gas streams, highlighting the power of programmed pore microenvironments to discriminate trace toxic species from abundant value-added molecules under chemically aggressive conditions.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
item.description:
Yiqun Zeng, Yang Yu, Xiangyuan Liu, Dongshun Ni, Baomin Wang, Jisheng Luo, Li Deng
The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

item.title: JACS: Solar Biorefinery: Stoichiometric Coproduction of Gluconic and Glucaric Acids and Impurity-Free Hydrogen from Lignocellulosic Biomass and Water
item.description:
Ding Wang, Zhaosong Wu, Xiantong Zheng, Zijian Huang, Lin Yao, Ping Wang, Xinqiang Wang, Jiaming Liu, et al.
Solar biorefinery serves as a game changer in the sustainable production of transportation fuels and value-added chemicals by capitalizing on sunlight, lignocellulosic biomass, and water. Central to this endeavor is the modulation of highly reactive, nonselective hydroxyl radicals to prevent undesired side reactions. Here, surface-hydroxylated nickel oxyphosphide works synergistically with one-dimensional gallium nitride, enabling the selective reforming of lignocellulose in water toward glucose-derived organic acids (GOAs: gluconic and glucaric acids) and H2 at a nearly stoichiometric ratio: (C6H12O6)n+ H2O + sunlight → GOAs + H2. The GaN@NiOP–OH system achieves an H2 evolution rate of 2.55 mol g–1 h–1 with 100% gas-phase selectivity under simulated concentrated sunlight at 3.5 W cm–2. GOAs are simultaneously produced at a total rate of 2.23 mol g–1 h–1, corresponding to a near-stoichiometric GOAs/H2 ratio of 0.97 with nearly 100% atom utilization efficiency. This platform is broadly applicable to sunlight-driven reforming of cellulose, straw, and camphorwood. In situ spectroscopy, isotope labeling, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that NiOP–OH cooperates with GaN to modulate in situ-generated hydroxyl radical species originating from water oxidation by photogenerated holes. These radicals are confined on the catalytic surface with their nonselective reactivity finely tuned, enabling selective conversion of glucose with H2O into GOAs and H2 via a dynamic hydroxyl exchange mechanism while suppressing side and mineralization reactions. Outdoor testing and techno-economic analysis confirm the practical viability of this proof-of-concept solar biorefinery for coproducing high-value chemicals and green H2 using only sunlight, lignocellulose, and water.

item.title: JACS: Photocatalytic Three-Component Radical Addition of Aromatic Compounds
item.description:
Huijun Qian, Jing Liu, Yuting Feng, Yujuan Gui, Xingwei Guo, Zhiping Li
Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.

item.title: JACS: High-Resolution 6Li Solid-State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Reveals Hidden Lithium Dynamics in All-Solid-State Cathodes
item.description:
Houyi Liu, Bao Zhang, Yuhao Duan, Jiuwei Lei, Wen Yin, Wei Xia, Hongzhang Zhang, Kuizhi Chen, et al.
The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control. This method resolves and quantifies three Li+ environments, revealing that local Li/Fe disorder drives in-place Fe2+ reduction as the root cause of highly reversible intercalation-conversion chemistry. It further uncovers trace irreversible Fe0 species invisible to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Guided by this hidden degradation signature, optimization of the voltage window enables 85.9% capacity retention after 500 cycles with a 16.3% energy-density penalty, whereas full-depth cycling retains 68.6% after 100 cycles. Our work establishes lithium-resolved NMR as a platform linking disorder, hidden redox, and reversibility in paramagnetic cathodes.

item.title: ACS Nano: Symmetry-Directed Engineering of Quantum Defects: Toward Monodispersed Organic Color Centers in Carbon Nanotubes
item.description:
Mengyue Wang, Jacob Fortner, Benjamin Barnes, Daichi Kozawa, Chee Fai Fong, Jeffrey A. Fagan, Yuichiro K. Kato, YuHuang Wang
Achieving spectrally uniform single-photon emission is crucial for scalable quantum photonics, yet conventional approaches often yield broad and unpredictable emission. Here, we report on the selective creation of organic color centers (OCCs) on high-symmetry zigzag (10,0) single-walled carbon nanotubes via a [2 + 2] cycloaddition reaction with 4-cyclopentene-1,3-dione. Density functional theory predicts two possible OCC binding configurations separated by >200 meV, favoring the selective formation of a single OCC geometry. Through chirality sorting, hyperspectral photoluminescence imaging, and multi-step spectral screening, we isolate functionalized (10,0) nanotubes and observe a substantially narrower distribution of OCC emission wavelengths than similarly functionalized chiral nanotubes. Time-resolved photoluminescence and photon correlation measurements further confirm single-photon emission at room temperature. These results demonstrate divalent OCCs on symmetric nanotubes as promising quantum emitters, offering a route toward scalable atomically defined light sources for integrated photonics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Unveiling the Structural Origin of Low-Frequency Noise in Organic Photodetectors
item.description:
Gyeong Min Lee, Ohhyun Kwon, Hyungju Ahn, Myung-Seok Lee, Jung-Hyun Lee, Han Jung Park, Jae Won Shim
Active-layer morphology critically shapes the low-frequency noise characteristics of organic photodetectors (OPDs), yet the mechanistic link between crystallization pathway and power spectral density (PSD) remains underexplored. This study demonstrates that solvent evaporation kinetics governs a crystallization sequence that determines low-frequency noise in PM6:Y6 ternary OPDs. Differential scanning calorimetry and surface-energy measurements show that L8-BO has an approximately 41% lower nucleation barrier than Y6, a thermodynamic hierarchy that places L8-BO as the preferentially nucleating component and directs fast-drying chloroform (CF) processing toward a seeded alloy formation route. This nucleation-seeded pathway produces a structurally uniform alloy-like acceptor phase with suppressed energetic disorder (17.9 meV) and low trap density (2.54 × 1012 cm–3). In contrast, slow-drying chlorobenzene (CB) promotes competitive dual-phase crystallization, increases trap density to approximately 4.98 × 1013 cm–3, and drives dark-current activation energy well below Eg/2, indicating shunt-like interfacial leakage. Lorentzian generation-recombination (G-R) noise analysis shows that the G-R roll-off frequency increases monotonically with reverse bias in CF-processed OPDs, consistent with Poole–Frenkel-enhanced Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) emission from well-localized midgap traps. This trap-kinetics-resolved PSD analysis establishes crystallization pathway engineering as a physically grounded strategy for noise-aware OPD design.

item.title: Nano Letters: Lipoprotein-Driven Remodeling of Interfacial Charge Governs Protein-Mediated Implant Integration
item.description:
Chengyue Ou, Fanyu Zhang, Junjia Wang, Muhesen Yashengjiang, Qunli Liu, Jiaqiang Zhang, Yian Shen, Tianman Wang, et al.
Hyperlipidemia compromises implant integration, but the molecular mechanisms linking dyslipidemic environments to the biomaterial performance remain largely unknown. Here, we identify interfacial charge remodeling as a key regulator of the protein-mediated cell adhesion. Fibronectin (FN) is shown to govern endothelial attachment under hyperlipidemic conditions through charge-dependent interactions with the material surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the local charge distribution governs FN adsorption and conformational stability, while total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) single-molecule tracking demonstrates that charged adhesion domains regulate FN residence and adhesion stability in lipoprotein-rich environments. Deletion of negatively charged residues stabilizes FN–surface interactions, attenuates lipid-dependent disruption of adhesion signaling, and enhances endothelial responses. Similar charge-dependent behavior is observed on poly(lactic acid) (PLA), extending this interfacial charge remodeling from inorganic to organic biomaterials. These findings establish interfacial charge as a molecular determinant of implant integration under hyperlipidemic conditions and provide a general strategy for designing metabolism-responsive biomaterials.

item.title: JACS: Visualizing B–N Bond Breaking in Silicone Elastomer Networks through Turn-On Mechanochromic Luminescence
item.description:
Beijia Chen, Fernando Vidal, Frieder Jäkle
Mechanochromic luminescence (MCL) plays important roles in sensors, encryption, as impact indicators, and in real-time stress mapping. Boron–nitrogen Lewis pairs (LPs) are promising as mechanophores because both the interaction energy and the luminescence color can be readily fine-tuned. However, elastomers based on luminescent organoboron polymers have yet to be explored. Mechanofluorochromic elastomers were prepared by cross-linking pyridyl-substituted poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) with luminescent polystyrene (PS)-based organoborane polymeric Lewis acids. Apart from enabling the full compatibilization of otherwise immiscible PS/PDMS matrices, supramolecular B–N bond formation quenched the blue emission of PS1 via complexation of its pendant bithiophenyl-substituted arylborane chromophore units with pyridyl-functionalized PDMS. Upon stretching of the polymer film, a fluorescence turn-on, corresponding to uncomplexed boron chromophores, was observed by the naked eye under UV irradiation, indicating that the mechanical force was effectively translated to cleave the dynamic B–N bond. Aided by the low Tg of the PDMS segments, the “frustrated” mechanofluorochromic Lewis pairs (MFLPs) recombined instantly upon stress relief, rendering the material nonfluorescent again. Use of a yellow-luminescent donor-π-acceptor fluorophore that turns blue-emissive after pyridyl binding in PS2 led to a ratiometric fluorescence response. Tensile tests and oscillatory rheology studies showed that network F1 was relatively stronger than network F2, consistent with the relative Lewis acid strengths and ligand exchange kinetics derived from studies on molecular model systems. These results demonstrate the potential of tunable B–N Lewis pairs as versatile mechanofluorochromic cross-links in polymer networks.

item.title: ACS Nano: Activity-Stability Balance Enabled by Orbital Splitting Energy in Ruthenium-Based Oxide Catalysts
item.description:
Qingyi Liu, Lifeng Hang, Jinwu Liu, Da-Qian Cai, Zhehan Yi, Tao Zhang, Ting Yu, Hong Jin Fan
Ruthenium oxides have been the model catalyst for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction. It has been a challenge to achieve both stability and activity and establish a comprehensive descriptor for Ru-based catalysts. Herein, guided by the ligand field theory, we introduce the Ru orbital splitting energy (ΔRu) as a quantitative parameter to describe the interaction between Ru 4d and O 2p orbitals to govern the overall catalytic performance. A series of two-dimensional (2D) multielement metal oxides are synthesized via a self-assembly method to modulate ΔRu. The optimized RuCoFeNiO catalyst for water oxidation delivers a current density of 10 mA cm–2 at a low overpotential of 180 mV and shows high activity for more than 2500 h at 1 A cm–2 in acidic condition. In situ measurements and theoretical analysis reveal that the surface hydrogen-bond network balances the amount of surficial two-hydrogen-bonded water and free water, boosting the proton-transfer process. Moreover, the optimized ΔRu (2.405 eV) modifies the adsorption of *OOH on Ru sites, switching the dominant reaction pathway from the lattice oxygen mediated mechanism to absorbate evolution mechanism. This work highlights the pivotal role of ΔRu in tailoring both stability and activity and may offer insights into high-entropy 2D Ru-based oxides as high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalysts.

item.title: JACS: A Pyridoxal 5′-Phosphate-Dependent Decarboxylative Mannich Reaction Initiates Construction of the Nonpeptidic Scaffold of Kaitocephalin
item.description:
Tomohiro Noguchi, Yukari Maeno, Kazuo Furihata, Kazuo Shin-ya, Tomohisa Kuzuyama
Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.

item.title: JACS: Tuning Second-Sphere Amine Basicity to Modulate Hydride Intermediates and Selectivity in Molecular Manganese Bipyridine CO2 Electroreduction
item.description:
Wanwan Hong, Ke Ye, Joakim B. Jakobsen, Lin Li, Clara Del Carmen-Rodríguez, Troels Skrydstrup, Steen U. Pedersen, Mårten S. G. Ahlquist, et al.
Manganese bipyridine tricarbonyl complexes represent a prominent class of molecular electrocatalysts for efficient and selective CO2-to-CO conversion. Recent efforts have sought to redirect product selectivity toward HCOOH by incorporating second-sphere amine proton relays. However, how the physicochemical properties of second-sphere amines govern catalytic activity and selectivity remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we report a new manganese bipyridine complex bearing 2-(pyrrolidin-1-ylmethyl)phenyl substituents at the 6,6′-positions and systematically evaluate its performance against the diethylamine- and morpholine-functionalized analogs to elucidate the role of second-sphere amine basicity on CO2 reduction. The pyrrolidine-functionalized catalyst achieves near-unity selectivity for HCOOH in acetonitrile with a Faradaic efficiency of 92%, outperforming the corresponding diethylamine (71%) and morpholine (23%) derivatives. This complex also displays outstanding catalytic activity with maximum turnover frequencies of 2300 s–1 and up to 70,000 s–1 under low- and high-overpotential conditions, respectively, ranking among the most active manganese bipyridine catalysts for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the pyrrolidine groups function as proton relays, facilitating proton transfer to the manganese center and promoting formation of the key Mn-hydride intermediate for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that the stronger basicity of the pyrrolidine functionality lowers the energy barriers for amine protonation and subsequent intramolecular proton transfer by 3–6 kcal mol–1 relative to the less basic diethylamine and morpholine analogs. Overall, this work establishes second-sphere amine basicity as a key molecular parameter for tuning both activity and product selectivity in the development of molecular CO2 reduction catalysts.

item.title: JACS: A Standalone Flavoprotein Monooxygenase Directs Divergent Tropolone Skeletal Editing through Baeyer–Villiger-Triggered Rearrangement
item.description:
Ziang Chen, Jiawang Liu, Songlin Bai, Xinjia Wang, Chen Zhang, Bingyu Liu, Xiangbing Qi, Youcai Hu
Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C–C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O–O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer–Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.

item.title: JACS: Tetrapyridophenazine-Based Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Sequential Photocatalysis and Continuous-Flow Synthesis
item.description:
Minghao Liu, Chensheng Wang, Yingguo Li, Honglin Wen, Zhiyao Li, Ju Liu, Mengmeng Fu, Xiaoyi Yue, et al.
Vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts because their conjugated sp2-carbon frameworks combine exceptional chemical stability with efficient charge transport. However, the limited reversibility of C═C bond formation narrows the scope of polymerizable monomers, restricting the structural diversity and electronic tunability of vinylene-linked COFs. Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on a planar, electron-deficient, nitrogen-rich tetrapyridophenazine (TTPhz) building block for constructing vinylene-linked COFs. Knoevenagel polycondensation of a polymerizable TTPhz monomer with aromatic dialdehydes affords three highly crystalline COFs with tunable donor–acceptor interactions and electronic structures. The optimized fluorinated framework, TTPhz-COF-3, exhibits efficient charge separation and transport, enabling a previously unreported one-pot sequential photocatalytic synthesis of 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran derivatives from arylboronic acids through tandem aerobic hydroxylation and oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition. The catalyst displays broad substrate scope, excellent recyclability, and enables gram-scale continuous-flow synthesis of a key intermediate of the natural product (±)-conocarpan with a 4-fold higher turnover frequency than the corresponding batch process. This work expands the structural and functional scope of vinylene-linked COFs and establishes molecular building-block design as a general strategy for developing advanced crystalline organic photocatalysts.

item.title: Nano Letters: Band Degeneracy and Liquid-like Dynamics in Intercalated La2O2Te/BiAgSeO Thermoelectrics
item.description:
Yufei Meng, Pengfei Zhang, Shulin Bai, Da Wan, Zhanpeng Xu, Hao Sun, Amondulloi Burhonzoda, Shuwei Tang, et al.
Interlayer modulation of layered oxychalcogenide superlattices provides a strategy to decouple electron–phonon transport for high-performance thermoelectric (TE) materials. Herein, an intercalated oxychalcogenide superlattice (La4Bi2Ag2Se2Te2O6) is theoretically designed by inserting a La2O2Te slab into the BiAgSeO framework to synergistically optimize carrier and phonon transport behaviors and systematically uncover an unprecedented synergy of orbital-driven valence band degeneracy and Ag+ liquid-like ionic dynamics. The La4Bi2Ag2Se2Te2O6 superlattice exhibits a highly anisotropic lattice architecture characterized by strong intralayer covalent bonding and weak interlayer interactions, which simultaneously preserves structural stability and promotes pronounced lattice anharmonicity. Meanwhile, stereochemically active Bi 6s2 lone-pair electrons, four-phonon scattering, and phonon–diffuson conversion drastically suppress the lattice thermal conductivity. This work establishes a dual-regulation intercalation paradigm combining band convergence and liquid-cation dynamics, offering a universal route for designing high-efficiency layered TE materials.

item.title: Nano Letters: A Thermoelectric Hydrogel-Based Insole with Self-Decoupled Temperature and Pressure Sensing for Diabetic Plantar Monitoring
item.description:
Yu Niu, Chunjing Wang, Saeed Ahmed Khan, Xinru Yang, Ning Li, Hao Chen, Yanrong Li, Dapeng Yang, et al.
Plantar temperature and pressure reflect the plantar health status of diabetic patients and serve as critical indicators for evaluating disease progression. However, existing plantar monitoring devices are still limited by single-modal signal acquisition, bulky device configurations, and a strong reliance on external power supplies. Herein, we report a thermogalvanic hydrogel-based smart insole integrating self-powered sensing units for self-decoupled plantar monitoring. The insole integrates 16 self-decoupled thermogalvanic hydrogel sensing units, which convert plantar temperature difference and pressure stimuli into decouplable electrical signals via the thermogalvanic effect and the active iontronic piezoresistive effect, respectively. The incorporation of the backend acquisition circuit into the smart monitoring insole enables remote plantar temperature-difference and pressure mapping. Cloud-based machine learning further empowers the insole to assess plantar status in diabetic patients and distinguish disease-associated gait patterns. This work provides a versatile strategy for developing multimodal intelligent wearable platforms for personalized foot health monitoring and disease management.

item.title: JACS: Multicomponent Nanocrystal Superlattice Structure Prediction from First-Principles Validated against Two Decades of Experiments
item.description:
Santiago F. Bonoli, Leandro L. Missoni, Yamila A. Perez Sirkin, Mario Tagliazucchi, Alex Travesset
Predicting nanocrystal (nanoparticle) assembly into ordered arrays (superlattices) is a grand challenge in materials chemistry that has largely resisted first-principles theories. Here, we extend MOLT-CF, a classical density functional theory, to multicomponent nanocrystal systems and subject it to a rigorous validation by comparing against nearly 300 experiments spanning two decades of literature. We use MOLT-CF to predict stability and phase diagrams for binary superlattices of nanocrystals with linear hydrocarbon ligands, as well as many other fine structural details, for example, lattice constants, packing fractions, ligand structure, and, in the case of (cubic) perovskite nanocrystals, orientation. Significant discrepancies from experiments are noted only for the Li3Bi and Cu3Au superlattices. In the former, we predict that this lattice is stabilized by particle fractionalization, which is supported by a reexamination of experimental data in the literature. In the case of Cu3Au (for which MOLT-CF predicts thermodynamic instability against phase separation into single-component lattices), we propose two alternative candidate structures that reconcile theory with experimental observations. These results establish MOLT-CF as a rigorous platform for the computational design of next-generation functional nanoparticle materials.

item.title: Nano Letters: Probing and Sensing Layer-Dependent van der Waals Interaction via Induced Anisotropy
item.description:
Ting Wen, Shuang Cai, Ziluo Su, Yalan Wang, Jiaqi Wu, Jiaze Qin, Chenyin Jiao, Zenghui Wang, et al.
Van der Waals (vdW) interaction, a fundamental force, plays an important role in two-dimensional (2D) systems by enabling atomically sharp assemblies and giving rise to many emergent phenomena. However, experimentally probing and sensing the evolution of vdW interaction between 2D layers remains challenging due to its extreme weakness, very short range, and the difficulty of keeping two atomic layers perfectly parallel while finely adjusting the interaction. Here, we demonstrate an optical strategy to indirectly probe vdW interactions by exploiting induced anisotropy in MoS2/NbIrTe4 heterostructures. We construct heterostructures using isotropic MoS2 and anisotropic NbIrTe4 to ensure perfect parallelism. We modulate and probe the vdW interaction by varying the NbIrTe4 thickness and monitor the vdW-interaction-induced anisotropy in MoS2. We find such induced anisotropy to strongly depend on the NbIrTe4 thickness and clearly observe its fast-decaying nature. This work provides a simple, noncontact approach for indirectly probing interlayer vdW interactions.

item.title: ACS Nano: Unified Single-Transistor Cell for Multimode Reconfigurable Logic and Ternary In-Memory Search
item.description:
Jiahui Lyu, Ji Hwan Lee, Jingjie Niu, Stanislav Sin, Nayeong Lee, Cheolhwa Jang, Koyal Suman Samantaray, Xiangyu Mi, et al.
The rapid growth of data-intensive applications demands efficient data processing with reduced data movement. Logic-in-memory (LIM) and in-memory search, exemplified by ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM), offer promising solutions; however, their typical implementation in separate device modules leads to increased circuit complexity and limited cell-level functional density. Here, we demonstrate a split-gate van der Waals ferroelectric field-effect transistor (vdW FeFET) as a unified operational cell for multimode reconfigurable logic and ternary in-memory search. The architecture integrates two parallel split gates, employing MoS2 as the channel and ferroelectric CuInP2S6 as the gate dielectric. Polarity-dependent modulation by the split gates and the drain bias enables multimode reconfigurable logic operation, supporting six Boolean functions, including directional data transfer. The same device can be programmed for associative memory equivalent to a one-transistor-per-cell TCAM, where two spatially separated ferroelectric regions are programmed within one continuous MoS2 channel, allowing ternary states to be stored and match and mismatch responses to be encoded directly into the channel current. Device-calibrated statistical simulations confirm ranking-based row discrimination under realistic device variability. By linking reconfigurable logic, spatial ferroelectric programming, and current-domain associative search within a common split-gate device framework, this work presents a compact transistor platform for logic-search-coupled in-memory computing.

item.title: JACS: Chemical Bonding Rules for Stacking-Sequence Stability in Bismuth Oxychloride Intergrowths and Their Consequences for Band Structure
item.description:
Nayana Christudas Beena, Varsha Kumari, Emily Ward, Megan Knobeloch, Alexandru B. Georgescu, Sara E. Skrabalak
Metal oxyhalides are versatile materials, exhibiting properties relevant to photocatalysis, solid-state battery systems, ferromagnetism, multiferroics, and nonlinear optics. Here, mixed-metal oxyhalide intergrowths, layered materials formed by intercalating SrBi3O4Cl3 and Bi2GdO4Cl blocks along the c direction within a crystal, are reported. They are synthesized through a flux-based approach in which the SrBi3O4Cl3-to-Bi2GdO4Cl ratio can be precisely controlled. Despite the structural and compositional flexibility of such intergrowths, there is no general framework for predicting which local structural arrangements are preferred. Density functional theory combined with Bader charge analysis shows that preferred stacking sequences are those that minimize charge disproportionation across distinct chlorine environments, consistent with Pauling’s fifth rule, and we support this bonding-based framework through computational cation substitution that shifts the ionic-covalent balance of the metal–chloride bonding. With the preferred stacking arrangement established, this same system further reveals that intergrowth layering and Sr/Bi site occupancy modulate the interaction between the Bi3+ lone pair and anion p orbitals. Density functional theory calculations reveal that intergrowth formation destabilizes the O-2p orbitals, raising the valence band maximum for visible-light absorption, with the lone-pair interaction and layering-driven internal electrostatic field acting as competing effects on the resulting band gap. Significantly, this experimental-computational study establishes a transferable, bonding-based framework for stacking-sequence stability in layered oxyhalide intergrowths, while also clarifying how the same structural levers used to control stability can be tuned to engineer band structure.

item.title: ACS Nano: Morphology and Ion Transport in Zwitterionic Polysiloxanes
item.description:
Harmandeep Singh, Dylan M. Barber, Shinian Cheng, Michelle Lehmann, Michael D. Nelwood, Jennifer A. Lewis, Alexei P. Sokolov
The recent discovery of superionic conductivity in doped polyzwitterions (PZIs) has opened a new direction for polymer electrolytes (PEs). Solid-state battery research is currently dominated by inorganic electrolytes due to their rigidity and high conductivity, but they suffer from poor electrode adhesion and processability issues. While PEs overcome these issues, they typically suffer from low ionic conductivity. Recently, salt-doped PZIs have emerged as promising candidates, where high concentrations of ionic species and local dipolar interactions can reduce energy barriers for ion transport and therefore increase room-temperature ionic conductivity. Here, we demonstrate that superionic conductivity is not a universal behavior of doped PZIs, but rather a strategic design of ion-transport pathways is required. Using a flexible polysiloxane-based PZI doped with LiTFSI salt, we observe that room-temperature conductivity remains limited (∼10–8 S/cm at 293 K) despite a relatively low glass transition temperature and high dielectric constant. X-ray scattering reveals the structural origin of this behavior; namely, zwitterionic groups aggregate into isolated nanodomains separated by the polymer matrix, which slows down ion mobility. Once these clusters start overlapping, doped PZI showed significant enhancement in conductivity. These results demonstrate the critical role of percolating ion channels for superionic conductivity in PZIs.

item.title: JACS: Direct Detection of the Calcium–Sodium–Calcium Metal Triad in Thermostable α-Amylases from Bacillus sp. Bacteria in Aqueous Solution by 23Na Quadrupole-Central-Transition NMR Spectroscopy
item.description:
Ziyao Peng, Gang Wu
We report that the Na+ ion within the calcium–sodium–calcium (Ca–Na–Ca) metal triad in two thermostable bacterial α-amylases (ca. 58 kDa) can be directly detected by 23Na (I = 3/2) quadrupole-central-transition (QCT) NMR spectroscopy in aqueous solution. We show that 23Na QCT NMR signals from hyperthermostable Bacillus licheniformis α-amylase (BLA) and its mesophilic homologue, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens α-amylase (BAA), exhibit remarkable subppm spectral resolution, which is unprecedented in NMR studies of quadrupolar nuclei in proteins. Using this new 23Na QCT NMR methodology, we examine the pH-dependent unfolding, melting temperatures (Tm), long-term thermal inactivation profiles, and chemical denaturing of BAA and BLA. We also use 23Na QCT NMR to monitor EDTA titration experiments, which yielded the apparent binding constants of the Na+ ion to BAA and BLA to be (0.3 ± 0.1) × 109 and (0.6 ± 0.1) × 109 M–1, respectively. Because the Ca–Na–Ca metal triad is located in the vicinity of the active cleft, the subppm spectral resolution of 23Na QCT NMR makes it possible to detect subtle changes of the enzyme structure caused by the presence of inhibitors such as acarbose and quercetin. This work represents the first time that Na+ ions tightly bound to an enzyme are directly observed by 23Na QCT NMR in aqueous solution. This new 23Na QCT NMR approach can potentially be extended to detection of other metal ions with quadrupolar nuclei such as K+, Mg2+, and Zn2+ in metalloenzymes in their native aqueous environment.

item.title: ACS Nano: Exclusive Detection of Dimethyl Sulfide by a Pd–WO3 Sensor with the CuO/Al2O3 Filtering Overlayer
item.description:
Ruofan Zhang, Xingxing Xie, Zanhong Deng, Jie Meng, Xiaohua Ji, Qi Zhang, Ruoqing Zhang, Siyuan Liu, et al.
Selective detection of trace (weakly reducing) dimethyl sulfide (DMS) in highly humid exhaled breath using metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors, with the presence of strong reducing H2S interference gas, is essential for the early diagnosis of hepatic diseases. However, it remains a big challenge in principle. Herein, a bilayer MOS sensor with a Pd–WO3 sensing film and a CuO/Al2O3 filtering overlayer was proposed. The temperature-dependent H2S catalytic oxidation experiment suggests that CuO could effectively filter H2S even under room temperature. Dispersing the CuO particles into insulative Al2O3 carrier could not only selectively remove H2S without significant consumption of DMS but also isolate the underlying Pd–WO3 sensing layer’s response signal from interference caused by that of CuO. By adding the CuO/Al2O3 1:9 filtering overlayer, the response ratio of DMS to H2S was significantly enhanced from 3.3 to 50.4, furthermore, an ultrahigh response (701.3) to 10 ppm DMS, and a low limit of detection of 10 ppb under 90% RH were achieved, which promises the future breath disease diagnosis.

item.title: JACS: Redox Properties of the Copper Centers in Particulate Methane Monooxygenase
item.description:
Divyansh Prakash, Joseph D. Groom, Frank J. Tucci, José M. Ayala, Mary E. Lidstrom, Amy C. Rosenzweig
Particulate methane monooxygenase (pMMO) and its homolog ammonia monooxygenase (AMO), central enzymes in the global carbon and nitrogen cycles, contain three highly conserved mononuclear copper centers, denoted CuB, CuC, and CuD. While these sites have been well characterized structurally and spectroscopically, with recent studies identifying CuD as the active site, their reduction potentials have not been measured. This knowledge gap has hindered efforts to determine how the two electrons and two protons required for substrate oxidation are sourced and delivered. Here, we have elucidated the redox properties of each copper center in pMMO/AMO by protein film voltammetry using samples with copper occupancies known from cryoelectron microscopy (cryoEM) structures. The reduction potential of the CuB site, −72 to −139 mV, is significantly lower than the ∼400 mV measured for the CuD site, with consistent values determined for pMMOs and AMO from different species. Mutation of a residue in the second sphere of CuB, Glu35, alters the redox potential and impairs cell growth and pMMO activity, indicating that redox chemistry at CuB might be functionally relevant. Finally, a Pourbaix diagram constructed for the CuBII/I and CuDII/I half-reactions suggests that a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process occurs at the CuD site but not at the CuB site. Thermochemical analysis of this proposed PCET process is compatible with electron delivery by a quinol reductant. These results provide new context for future investigations of the pMMO and AMO reaction mechanisms.

item.title: Nano Letters: Broadband Near-Field Imaging of Strong Polariton Coupling in Graphene/CrI3 Heterostructures
item.description:
Zijian Zhou, Chun-Chih Tseng, Wenjun Zheng, Heng Wang, Heze Zhao, Christopher C. Homes, G. L. Carr, D. N. Basov, et al.
Interfacial charge transfer in van der Waals heterostructures provides a powerful, contact-free mechanism to activate two-dimensional plasmons. Chromium iodide (CrI3), a layered ferromagnetic insulator, induces significant doping in adjacent graphene, yet its nanoscale polaritonic response and the optical manifestation of this charge transfer remain unexplored. Here, we report the direct real-space observation of propagating graphene surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) sustained entirely by spontaneous interfacial charge transfer at the graphene/CrI3 interface. Interestingly, a distinct polaritonic anticrossing near 214 cm–1 (6.4 THz) between the charge-transfer-induced graphene SPP and the CrI3 phonon is identified, suggesting this hybrid system lies within the strong-coupling regime. Our work is enabled by the recent advances in broadband synchrotron near-field nanospectroscopy and suggests intriguing opportunities for magnetically switchable polaritonics in the hybrid charge-transfer heterostructures.

item.title: Nano Letters: Atomic-Scale Mapping of an Emergent Interfacial Two-Dimensional Electron Gas at Anatase/LaAlO3
item.description:
Michael Oberaigner, Manuel Ederer, Sandeep K. Chaluvadi, Pasquale Orgiani, Regina Ciancio, Stefan Löffler, Gerald Kothleitner, Daniel Knez
Atomic-level insight into structure, charge distribution, chemistry, and electronic states is essential for understanding emergent properties at oxide interfaces. Here, we leverage the quasi-strain-free anatase TiO2/LaAlO3 interface as an ideal model system to decouple intrinsic polar discontinuities from complex strain artifacts. By combining atomic-resolution electron energy loss spectroscopy with integrated differential phase contrast, we spatially map the electronic states associated with the formation of a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG). This correlative approach enables the direct real-space disentanglement of intrinsic 2DEG-related states from extrinsic Ti3+ defect states. Supported by density functional theory and inelastic scattering simulations, we reveal a physical superposition: the intrinsic polar electronic reconstruction anchors metallic states directly at the boundary, while oxygen vacancies accumulate further into the film, acting as a donor reservoir. This work not only resolves long-standing ambiguities regarding oxide interfacial conductivity but also provides a robust, transferable framework for related material systems.

item.title: JACS: Clickable Photolabile Linkers for Convenient Immobilization and Light-Controlled Release of Substrates from Solid Support
item.description:
Selvanathan Arumugam, Nannan Lin, Chen Zhao, Jin Xie, Vladimir V. Popik
Photolabile linkers (PLLs) enable spatiotemporal control over substrate release but often suffer from slow photorelease kinetics, low quantum yields, or limited functionalization options. Here, we report a family of heterobifunctional PLLs based on (3-hydroxy-5-alkoxynaphthalen-2-yl)methyl (NQMP) chromophores that combine rapid, high-yielding photochemical cleavage with orthogonal conjugation chemistries for efficient substrate immobilization and light-triggered release. Six heterobifunctional NQMP-based linkers bearing terminal acetylene, cyclooctyne, amine, carboxyl, allyl, and biotin groups were synthesized and employed for the immobilization of fluorescent dyes, acetylsalicylic acid, biotin, avidin, and doxorubicin on silica microspheres and mesoporous silica nanoparticles. Mild UV-A irradiation resulted in efficient release of the attached payloads while preserving the integrity of the solid support. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles provide high loading capacity and are suitable for light-controlled drug delivery. The modular design, excellent photochemical efficiency, orthogonal conjugation chemistries, and compatibility with diverse substrates make NQMP-based PLLs versatile tools for reversible surface functionalization, controlled cargo release, affinity capture, and photoresponsive drug delivery applications.

item.title: Nano Letters: Buoyancy-Mediated in Situ Phase-Transition Microbubbles Enable Efficient Aqueous Humor Drug Delivery for Accelerated Corneal Endothelial Regeneration
item.description:
Shundong Cai, Mengdie Li, Jingbin Zhuang, Meiqin Zhong, Mingyou Zhang, Xu Hu, Jinfa Ye, Yun Han, et al.
The corneal endothelium plays a pivotal role in maintaining corneal clarity, and its damage leads to a hydration dysfunction and secondary glaucoma. We previously identified XMU-MP-1, a Hippo pathway inhibitor, as a potent stimulator of corneal endothelial cell proliferation in nonhuman primate models. However, its therapeutic potential is limited by poor intraocular permeability and low bioavailability. Herein, we report an engineered perfluoropentane (PFP)-cored lipid microbubble (MB) platform for the buoyancy-mediated targeted delivery of XMU-MP-1. Post intracameral injection, drug-loaded microbubbles (D@MB) undergo spontaneous in situ liquid-to-gas phase transition at physiological temperature, which grants them buoyancy-driven upward movement in aqueous humor to maintain continuous direct contact with the endothelial layer, achieving an extended retention of over 72 h in the anterior chamber. Finally, the D@MB drug delivery platform accelerates regenerative processes and restores both the corneal ultrastructure and physiological function. This study highlights a minimally invasive approach that bypasses traditional surgical interventions to stimulate the repair of the damaged corneal endothelium.

item.title: JACS: Catalytic Asymmetric 1,6-Diene Cyclization via Designed Carbocationic 5- and 6- exo Pathways
item.description:
Xiang Liu, Tianteng Zhao, Junjie Li, Qingxiang Cao, Fuming Zhong, Lihao Liao, Qian Peng, Xiaodan Zhao
Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. Despite significant progress in this field, the asymmetric functionalization of alkenes promoted by an electrophilic carbon species via an exo-cyclization mode remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a solution to this challenge: alkenes can undergo designed 5-exo- and 6-exo-carbocationic cyclizations to generate optically pure, complex chiral compounds with high enantio- and diastereoselectivities. In this approach, for 1,6-dienes bearing bulky sulfonamide or quaternary carbon linkers, one double bond of the substrate interacts with an external electrophile, such as a trifluoromethylthio, arylthio, alkylthio, or chlorine species, generating an electrophilic carbon species that promotes the transformation of 1,6-dienes under chiral indane-based chalcogenide catalysis. Notably, the reaction can be terminated by intramolecular nucleophiles via cis-addition or can be captured by various intermolecular nucleophiles. A diverse array of optically pure polycyclic and monocyclic compounds can be obtained, including 5-5-6 tricyclic N-heterocycles and pentasubstituted chiral cyclohexanes. The same strategy can also be efficiently applied to 6-endo cyclizations, leading to the formation of 6-6-6 tricyclic and monocyclic N-heterocycles. The resulting products can be readily converted to various other valuable compounds, further demonstrating the utility of this methodology. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to rationalize the observed selectivities, revealing that the preferential transition-state conformations lower the activation barriers for the desired cyclization pathways. This work offers a versatile platform for the synthesis of enantioenriched chiral scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules and pharmaceuticals, significantly expanding the scope of polyene cyclization chemistry.

item.title: JACS: Imaging of Electrochemically Programmed Single-Molecule Reactions
item.description:
Cong-Hui Xu, Yu-Chao Song, Jing-Jing Zhang, Xi-Zhe Sun, Wei Zhao
Single-molecule reactions reveal intrinsic heterogeneity that is obscured in ensemble measurements. However, most existing approaches rely on extreme dilution, ultrasmall solution volumes, or physical confinement to keep individual events sufficiently sparse. Here, we introduce electrochemically programmed single-molecule reactions (PSMR), a pulse-regulated strategy that shifts single-molecule electrochemistry from passive observation to active control. It converts continuous interfacial reactions to a sequence of short, repeatable reaction trials. By tailoring the pulse waveform, PSMR controls the driving force and duration of each reaction trial, thereby regulating the probability of single-molecule reactions, while the relaxation interval between pulses allows the interface to recover before the next trial. This coordinated control enables single-molecule reactions to be actively regulated under conventional solution volumes and reaction concentrations. By coupling individual reaction events to single-photon emission through electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL), we can directly count and image the reactions. The ultrashort reaction windows and relaxation periods suppress diffusion-layer buildup, thereby preserving sensitivity to local reaction kinetics, even at high overpotentials. Using this approach, individual Au nanoparticles were imaged over a broad potential range, and particles as small as 5 nm were distinguished from the substrate background. Sparse photon events were accumulated over repeated trials and further analyzed using localization- and fluctuation-based algorithms, enabling super-resolution mapping of reaction activity beyond the optical diffraction limit. PSMR therefore provides a framework for actively regulating, quantitatively imaging, and spatially mapping single-molecule electrochemical reactions at nanointerfaces, opening new opportunities for mechanistic studies and rational design across molecular electrochemistry, electrocatalysis, and energy conversion.

item.title: Nano Letters: Regulating Chemomechanical Interactions in a High-Compaction Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 Cathode for Durable Sodium Storage
item.description:
Xu Wang, Yi Zhang, Jiahao Gu, Wen Zhou, Xiaodong Li, Yanqing Lai, Zhian Zhang
The polyanionic Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) cathode is recognized for its cost-effectiveness and three-dimensional framework structure. However, its anisotropic lattice evolution induces internal stress accumulation. Furthermore, the pursuit of high energy density necessitates high-compaction processing, which exacerbates localized stress buildup. Herein, this study explores and regulates the chemomechanical interactions of NFPP under high-compaction conditions. The formation of microcracks and new reaction interfaces constitutes a chemomechanical failure pathway. To suppress this, the introduction of large-sized La promotes grain refinement and close packing, thereby enhancing mechanical strength. Meanwhile, lattice substitution triggers local FeO6 structural rearrangement, strengthening the Fe–O bonds and mitigating lattice strain. The optimized NFPP-La exhibits a remarkable reversible capacity of 90.4 mAh g–1 at 10 C and retains 92.2% capacity after 5000 cycles under high compaction conditions. Moreover, pouch cell evaluation validated its outstanding temperature adaptability (−40 to 60 °C) and robust cycling stability.
