item.title: Nano Letters: Twist-Induced Out-of-Plane Ferroelectricity in Bilayer Hafnia
item.description:
Jian Huang, Gwan Yeong Jung, Pravan Omprakash, Guodong Ren, Xin Li, Xilong Xu, Du Li, Xiaoshan Xu, et al.
Ferroelectric HfO2 is a promising candidate for next-generation memory devices due to its CMOS compatibility and ability to retain polarization at nanometer scales. However, the polar orthorhombic phase responsible for ferroelectricity is metastable and requires extrinsic stabilization, complicating integration with silicon. Here, we predict that twist-induced symmetry breaking in bilayer 1T-HfO2 enables robust, switchable out-of-plane (OOP) polarization. First-principles density functional theory shows that monolayer 1T-HfO2, cleaved from the (111) surface of cubic HfO2, is dynamically stable. Twisting two aligned monolayers forms a moiré superlattice that breaks interlayer symmetry and yields bistable OOP polarization. At a twist angle of 7.34°, the bilayer exhibits ∼16 μC/cm2 polarization, primarily from polar displacements within AB stacking domains. The polarization can be switched via interlayer sliding with a low energy barrier (∼8 meV per formula unit), enabling electric-field tunability in atomically thin ferroelectric devices.

item.title: Nano Letters: Managing Proton-Involved Kinetics via Cooperative Acceptance and Diffusion of Protons for Stable Acidic Water Oxidation under Fluctuating Power
item.description:
Zhongfeng Wang, Mingming Wang, Hao Luo, Shaoyan Wang, Xiao Zhao
Practical application of RuO2 for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by its sluggish kinetics and serious degradation. Here, we manage proton-involved kinetics via cooperative acceptance and diffusion of protons by constructing CrOx islands on the RuO2 surface. This architecture renders two distinct yet spatially coupled functions: interfacial Cr–OH groups at the perimeters act as proton acceptors to promote the deprotonation of OER intermediates, while the hydroxyl-rich CrOx islands dynamically restructure interfacial water networks with potentials to facilitate proton diffusion away from catalyst-electrolyte interfaces. This enhances the OER kinetics but, more critically, reduces the local acidification to secure operational stability under fluctuating power. Water electrolyzers with this CrOx/RuO2 need a low voltage of 1.61 V at 1 A cm–2 and operate for over 1600 h under square-wave loading conditions (cycling between 0.1 and 1 A cm–2, each for 12 h), exceeding that using RuO2 (stability <12 h).

item.title: ACS Nano: Breaking the High-Voltage Limit of Na2CO3 Presodiation: An Interfacial Engineering Approach to Ampere-Hour Sodium-Ion Devices
item.description:
Luoming Zhang, Biao Zhong, Xinyu Zhang, Yuming Liu, Junpu Zhang, Bo Xiong, Shengrui Gao, Dongxiao Li, et al.
Na2CO3 is a promising sacrificial presodiation agent owing to its high capacity, excellent air stability, and low cost. However, its practical application is severely hampered by a high decomposition overpotential (>4.3 V vs Na/Na+), inducing detrimental electrolyte oxidation and cell degradation. To break this high-voltage limit, we propose an in situ interfacial dual-modification strategy, synergistically introducing interfacial oxygen vacancies and triggering electronic reconstruction, which thermodynamically lowers the reaction Gibbs free energy and kinetically diminishes the activation barriers, resulting in a dramatically reduced decomposition potential by 350 mV. Operando three-electrode diagnostics within a full sodium-ion capacitor reveal that this interface engineering not only facilitates efficient Na+ release (496.9 mAh g–1) at lower potential but also reduces the actual working potential of cathode, thereby fundamentally avoiding high-voltage parasitic reactions, according well with the DEMS and TOF-SIMS results. Consequently, the full cell achieves a considerable 117.4% enhancement in energy density. Most importantly, this strategy demonstrates compelling practicality in ampere-hour-level devices, delivering a substantial 22.4% boost in energy density with only 3 wt % additive in 1.5 Ah pouch cells. This work bridges microscopic interfacial chemistry and macroscopic device performance, providing a scalable and efficient blueprint for low-potential presodiation toward high-energy-density sodium-ion devices.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric Elongation of Uranyl within a Silver Nanocluster
item.description:
Liwei Cheng, Xing Dai, Lucia Amidani, Boyang Song, Chunyun Yang, Stephan Weiss, Chengyu Liang, Yu He, et al.
Confinement within nanoscale cavities can profoundly alter molecular structure and electronic properties, but this strategy has never been applied to inherently linear and symmetric uranyl cations (UO22+). Here, we report the first example of uranyl encapsulation within a self-assembled silver nanocluster, [UO2F5@Ag21(CCBut)14](BF4)3F (CCBut = 3,3-dimethyl-1-butynyl), abbreviated as UO2F5@Ag21. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals asymmetric elongation of the axial O ≡ U≡O bonds from the ideal symmetric value of 1.77 Å to 1.788(9) and 1.837(9) Å, respectively. Raman and IR spectroscopy show extreme redshifts of both symmetric and asymmetric stretching vibrations (ν1 down to 765 cm–1). Transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals an excited-state quenching process of the (UO2F5)3– guest driven by unique confinement. High-energy-resolved fluorescence detected X-ray absorption near edge structure (HERFD-XANES) at the U M4 edge demonstrates re-engineered 5f electronic states, with a shifted and broadened 5fσ* feature indicating reduced U≡O covalency. This work establishes nanoconfinement as a powerful new route to reshape the electronic structure and property of actinide-based materials.

item.title: Nano Letters: Tunable Nonlinear Landscapes in Graphene Nanoelectromechanical Systems
item.description:
Ateesh K. Rathi, Rajan Singh, Javed A. Mondal, Arnab Sarkar, Ryan J. T. Nicholl, Kirill I. Bolotin, Saikat Ghosh
Nonlinear nanomechanical resonators give convenient solid-state access to classical analogs of extreme nonlinear optics and to phononic signal processing. Here we report integer harmonic generation, phononic frequency sideband comb, and reverse period-doubling dynamics in a single platform of a suspended graphene resonator. A gate voltage breaks the out-of-plane symmetry of the membrane and establishes a 1:2 internal resonance between mechanical resonators. Under a single drive tone, integer harmonics are generated sequentially, forming a dense sideband frequency comb at larger drive. Raising the drive further, we find a reverse period-doubling transition: the comb spacing doubles, the line density halves, and energy flows back into the even-order comb lines. The measured spectrum yields the quadratic (ζ) and cubic (β) nonlinear coefficients of the membrane. These results demonstrate electrical control of several nonlinear landscapes in a single graphene resonator, enabling frequency multiplication, sideband comb generation, and broadband irregular motion.

item.title: JACS: On-Surface Synthesis of a Low Bandgap Cyclopenta[ c , d ]azulene-Based Polymer
item.description:
S. Jiménez-Fernández, F. Villalobos, V. Kumar, J. I. Martínez, J. I. Mendieta-Moreno, P. L. de Andrés, E. Tosi, J. A. Martín-Gago, et al.
Nonbenzenoid topologies offer a compelling strategy to tailor the electronic properties of low-dimensional carbon materials. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis of a nonalternant polymer incorporating a [7–5–5] cyclopenta[c,d]azulene (CPA) motif on Au(111) via thermally induced Ullmann coupling. Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy confirms the robustness of the [7–5–5] framework. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy, together with dI/dV mapping supported by density functional theory calculations, reveals a remarkable narrow polymeric bandgap of 1.5 eV. The electronic structure is governed by the intramolecular charge transfer from the heptagonal ring to the adjacent fused pentagonal rings, resulting in a pronounced dipole moment despite being composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen. Aromaticity analyses indicate the coexistence of locally aromatic and slightly antiaromatic regions, highlighting the intrinsic electronic frustration associated with the nonalternant topology. These findings demonstrate how the controlled incorporation of [7–5–5] motifs enables the rational bandgap engineering in carbon-based polymers and expands the scope of nonbenzenoid design in on-surface synthesis.

item.title: JACS: Tailoring Superhydrophobic Ultramicropores in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Humidity-Resistant Methane Purification
item.description:
Jialiang Liu, Chengtao Gong, Shuxin Yuan, Pengyue Hao, Xiaohui Li, Yongwu Peng
Efficient purification of methane from raw natural gas under humid conditions remains challenging because water adsorption often degrades the separation performance and structural stability of porous adsorbents. Here we report a topology- and stacking-guided molecular design strategy that integrates ultramicropore engineering with pore-surface fluorination to construct superhydrophobic covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for humidity-resistant methane purification. Two isoreticular fluorinated COFs, TF-COF and NF-COF, were constructed by rationally controlling framework topology and interlayer stacking, generating well-defined ultramicropores for size-selective discrimination of C1–C3 hydrocarbons. Fluorination simultaneously enhances pore-wall hydrophobicity and strengthens host–guest interactions, creating a confined adsorption environment that promotes hydrocarbon recognition while effectively suppressing competitive water adsorption. As a result, NF-COF exhibits a propane uptake of 99.4 cm3 g–1 and an exceptional C3H8/CH4 IAST selectivity of 251.7 at 298 K. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further demonstrate efficient methane purification under both dry and highly humid conditions, with the separation performance fully retained at 97% relative humidity owing to its superhydrophobic surface. Theoretical calculations reveal that densely distributed fluorine atoms generate synergistic pore confinement and multiple C–H···F van der Waals interactions, simultaneously maximizing adsorption capacity and molecular discrimination. These findings establish fluorinated superhydrophobic COFs as a robust platform for energy-efficient natural gas upgrading under industrially relevant humid conditions.

item.title: JACS: The Molecular Logic of Platelet-Activating Factor (PAF)
item.description:
Xiao Corey Ma, Jon Clardy
Platelet-activating factor (PAF) is a well-known if enigmatic lipid signal with important roles in inflammatory responses, allergic reactions, autoimmune diseases, and thrombotic cascades. Several lines of evidence suggest that our current model of PAF’s molecular mechanism is inadequate. This report describes a recontextualized model for PAF. The revised model embeds PAF in a plasmalogen-based molecular mechanism in which activation is a spontaneous chemical reaction triggered by environmental conditions that liberates a PAF receptor (PAF-R) agonist from a membrane-bound phospholipid. The active ligand subsequently undergoes a thermodynamically driven spontaneous rearrangement into an inactive isomer, a feature that controls response lifetime. The revised model is a molecule-autonomous set of transformations that create a response with spatial and temporal control. More generally the revised model’s congruence with a similar model for RORγt supports a picture in which plasmalogens form a part of the immune system that is separate from the cell-based innate and adaptive immune systems.

item.title: JACS: Unlocking the Tertiary Nitrogen Effect in 3D Anisotropic Covalent Organic Frameworks to Achieve Record Iodine Capture under Industrial Conditions
item.description:
Yuanzhe Jia, Liecheng Guo, Haifeng Zhang, Haoran Chu, Han Ren, Yuting Yang, Mian Li, Lele Gong, et al.
Using porous adsorbents to achieve efficient capture of radioactive iodine from nuclear waste under industrial conditions remains a formidable challenge, since most adsorbents just exhibit a low iodine uptake under such conditions. We herein show two 3D [8 + 4]-assembled covalent organic frameworks (COFs, ECUT-COF-99 and ECUT-COF-100) for this challenging target. The two COFs feature a minimal-transitivity [3 4] flu-derived net, which allows anisotropic isoreticular expansion through a general sequential derived-net approach. ECUT-COF-100 was found to give an ultrahigh iodine uptake of 1.51 g/g under simulated industrial conditions (150 °C and 150 ppmv I2), 5.2-fold that of ECUT-COF-99 (0.29 g/g). Such performance also far exceeds all established organic adsorbents for this use. Mechanism studies reveal that nonaromatic tertiary nitrogen atoms allow for strong charge transfer from the lone-pair electrons of tertiary nitrogen to I2, leading to the formation of ionic iodides (I3– and I5–) and the N·+ radical cation and then fixing of ionic iodides by Coulomb interactions. This work not only provides a promising adsorbent with record iodine uptake for radioactive iodine capture from nuclear waste but also highlights a new insight into the tertiary nitrogen effect in 3D COFs for efficient iodine capture.

item.title: JACS: Reactivity and Selectivity of Photocatalytic Nitrate Reduction Reaction to Ammonia: Pt, Pd, Ir, and Rh Single Atoms on p-Type TiO2 Nanotubes
item.description:
Hayoon Jung, Johannes Will, Michal Langer, Rostislav Langer, Štěpán Kment, Michal Otyepka, Erdmann Spiecker, Patrik Schmuki
We present a systematic study of noble metal (Pt, Pd, Ir, and Rh) single-atom cocatalysts decorated on p-type and quantum-confined TiO2 nanotubes for photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia. All single-atom cocatalysts were prepared through a reactive deposition using different metal precursors, resulting in a single-atom oxidation state (δ+) of δ ≈ 2. At a similar loading concentration (0.2–0.3 at%) and in the absence of any sacrificial agent, Pd single atoms exhibit the highest element-specific activity for ammonia production, while Pt single atoms display a prominent photocatalytic activity with a strong tendency of nitrite reduction toward ammonia. Rh single atoms achieve the highest ammonia selectivity, whereas Ir single atoms predominantly produce nitrite due to inhibited subsequent reduction. Comparisons with single atoms deposited on conventional TiO2 (P25) and with nanoparticles supported on the nanotubes reveal that both the semiconductor properties (quantum confinement effect and p-type conductivity) and the speciation of the cocatalyst (single atom) can significantly enhance activity and selectivity. These findings aid in establishing design principles for different single-atom catalysts toward efficient and selective photocatalytic nitrogen valorization.

item.title: ACS Nano: Single-Molecule Studies Reveal That Water Starts to Protect Proteins Even at the ppm Level
item.description:
Jiulong Zhou, Yan Wang, Ziyi Wang, Peng Zheng, Shuxun Cui
A consensus established by extensive thermodynamic and structural studies of proteins and DNA is that water acts as an indispensable structural cofactor rather than a passive solvent for biomolecules. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether trace water still exerts a stabilizing effect on proteins under ultradry conditions. Nonpolar organic solvents that spontaneously absorbed trace water provide an ideal platform to investigate this issue. Herein, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based single-molecule force spectroscopy (SMFS) was employed to investigate the mechanical behaviors of two model polyproteins, (GB1)8 and (I27)8, in nonpolar organic solvents with varying water contents. It was found that even at the ppm level, water protects protein stability and acts as a molecular switch: polyproteins fully denature at water contents ≤80 ppm (nonane and tetradecane), while metastable folded fragments can be retained at water contents ≥95 ppm (tetrachloroethane (TCE) and octane) with a characteristic unfolding force of approximately 100 pN. Force-free molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a smaller (I27)2 model in TCE further suggested that trace water accumulated preferentially around the protein, reorganizing the local solvation environment, thereby serving as a stabilizer. Based on the SMFS results, the water-content range of 80–95 ppm was identified as a critical threshold, across which polyproteins toggle between fully denatured and partially stabilized states. This work reveals the protective effect of trace water on proteins, quantifies its stabilizing capacity down to the ppm level, and offers insights for protein storage and astrobiology research.

item.title: Nano Letters: All-Optical Ultrafast Pure Spin Current in the Altermagnet Cr2SO
item.description:
Deepika Gill, Ruikai Wu, Wenhan Chen, Peter Elliott, Sangeeta Sharma, Sam Shallcross
All-optical generation of pure spin current─the flow of spin in the absence of a corresponding charge flow─relies on symmetry based compensation between the two spin channels. 2D d-wave altermagnets, which in many respects are ideal spintronic materials due to their very low spin–orbit coupling, possess a magnetic point group and highly anisotropic valley manifolds that would appear to preclude such current compensation, excluding them as materials for the ultrafast generation of pure spin current. Here we show that infrared valley excitation combined with a THz pulse envelope allows the generation of large and nearly 100% pure spin currents in the 2D altermagnet Cr2SO. Our approach is based on a valley selection rule coupling linearly polarized light to opposite spin valleys, along with the intrinsic momentum shift that a co-occurring THz pulse imbues a valley spin excitation with. These results provide a practical and all-optical route to the generation of pure spin current in 2D d-wave altermagnets, opening a path to lightwave control of spin in an environment with very low intrinsic spin–orbit coupling.

item.title: JACS: Redox-Induced Polymeric Micelle-to-Coacervate Transition for Enhanced Endosomal Escape, Prolonged Drug Retention, and Improved Sequential Drug Delivery
item.description:
Jiajia Ying, Jiafeng Wang, Zimeng Liu, Yinqi Chen, Yufei Nie, Yuliang Huang, Jiaxing Feng, Xuefei Zhou, et al.
Polymeric micelles (PMs) and coacervate microdroplets (CMs) are both promising delivery vehicles, yet each suffers from distinct limitations. The delivery efficiency of PMs is often hindered by factors, such as limited endosome escape and uncontrolled drug release. On the other hand, CMs are prone to coalescence and aging, which hamper long-term storage and systemic injection. Here, by employing an intracellular morphological transition strategy, these drawbacks can be efficiently addressed without compromising their inherent advantages. The system exists as nanosized PMs during storage and circulation. Upon internalization by the tumor cells, the highly reductive intracellular environment induces the detachment of the poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) shell and results in in situ formation of CMs. The formed CMs can effectively escape from endosomes by disrupting the endosomal membrane, facilitating the release of drugs into the cytoplasm. Furthermore, the CMs can serve as drug reservoirs, protecting the cargo from burst release and degradation, thus significantly prolonging the retention time and improving systemic delivery efficacy. Notably, the CMs can also sequester free drugs from the surrounding environment, enhancing sequential therapy by increasing the intratumoral accumulation of the temporally staggered agents. Thus, this micelle-to-coacervate transformable platform illuminates new possibilities for both types of drug-delivery systems.

item.title: JACS: Kinetic Programming of Heteromolecular Contacts in Boron- and Nitrogen-Containing π-Systems via External and Internal Cross-Seeding
item.description:
Shintaro Hasegawa, Soichiro Ogi, Shigehiro Yamaguchi
We establish a kinetic strategy for controlling the supramolecular copolymerization of boron- and nitrogen-containing π-electron systems by exploiting intramolecular hydrogen bonding in cystine-based dimeric diamides. Two dimeric diamides bearing solubilizing alkyl chains, DBB and DNN, were designed and synthesized by functionalization with planarized triarylborane (PTAB) and planarized triarylamine (PTAA) units, respectively. In low-polarity solvents, both molecules form one-dimensional nanostructures upon ultrasonication. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the two diamide units within the cystine framework suppresses spontaneous nucleation and generates metastable monomeric states, thereby providing a kinetic window for seeded supramolecular polymerization. Despite a difference of more than 10 kJ mol–1 between their Gibbs free energy changes for homopolymerization, external cross-seeding with preformed DBB seeds initiates the supramolecular polymerization of metastable DNN monomers. The resulting supramolecular copolymers exhibit long-lived emission arising from spatially confined interactions between the PTAB and PTAA units. The extent of heteromolecular contact formation can be modulated by switching between external and internal cross-seeding protocols. In the internal cross-seeding process, DBB assemblies are generated in situ in the presence of DNN monomers, enabling their incorporation during supramolecular growth and producing coassemblies with an enhanced contribution of heteromolecular excited-state interactions. These results demonstrate that kinetic control over nucleation and elongation enables pathway-dependent regulation of heteromolecular contacts in equimolar binary supramolecular polymers with markedly different homopolymerization propensities.

item.title: JACS: Giant Baromagnetic Effect Induced by Spin Engineering in Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C
item.description:
Jiechen Luo, Wentao Wu, Ao Qiu, Bing Wang, Xiuliang Yuan, Shihai An, Zhijie Ma, Zihui Xu, et al.
Baromagnetic effect (BME), arising from pressure-induced spin reorientation, holds great potential for next-generation information technologies owing to its strong multifield coupling characteristics. However, the practical implementation of BME is hindered by the small magnetization change and the large driving pressure required in conventional materials. Guided by spin-polarized calculations, this work successfully obtains a giant BME material Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C, which exhibits a remarkable pressure-induced maximum magnetization change (|ΔMmax|) of 2.63 μB·f.u.–1 and an exceptionally large baromagnetic coefficient (BMC, d) of 15.0 μB·f.u.–1·GPa–1. Temperature-dependent neutron powder diffraction (NPD) measurements reveal a clear evolution from the nearly collinear antiferromagnetic (cAFM) configuration with k = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2) to the ferromagnetic (FM) configuration, indicating that the spins are highly susceptible to reorientation under external perturbations. First-principles calculations further clarify that pressure modulates the energy difference (ΔE) between the cAFM and FM configurations via the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, elucidating the microscopic origin of the giant BME. This demonstration establishes spin engineering, achieved through precise control of spin configurations via targeted element selection, as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance baromagnetic systems. It further provides clear guidance for designing materials with superior functional properties.

item.title: JACS: Group Theory-Guided Orbital Symmetry Engineering of cis -Quinacridone: From Symmetry-Forbidden to Dipole-Allowed Transitions for Efficient Narrowband Emissions
item.description:
Zhijie Li, Ke Du, Xian-Kai Chen, Yayin Deng, Yuxuan He, Jingsong You, Zhengyang Bin
Although group theory is widely used to analyze symmetry and electronic transition selection rules in condensed matter physics and coordination chemistry, its use as a predictive design tool for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) remains largely unexplored. This is particularly important for highly symmetric emitters, where orbital-symmetry constraints can render the lowest-energy transition symmetry-forbidden. Herein, guided by quantum-chemical and group-theoretical analyses, we revisit the long-known cis- and trans-quinacridone isomers and reveal that the lowest-energy transition of cis-quinacridone (cis-QA) is symmetry-forbidden, resulting in a negligible transition dipole moment and intrinsically weak emission. We address this limitation through a group theory-guided orbital-symmetry engineering strategy based on carbonyl-to-imine transformation of the cis-QA skeleton. This targeted structural modification reorganizes the frontier orbital symmetry, converting the lowest-energy transition from symmetry-forbidden to dipole-allowed, while preserving the rigid, highly symmetric molecular framework and suppressing excited-state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling. The resulting cis-I2A2 derivatives exhibit high photoluminescence quantum yields (ΦPL) of 70–99% and narrow emission bandwidths with full-widths at half-maximum (fwhm’s) of 20–32 nm. An OLED based on cis-I2A2-3 delivers narrowband yellow electroluminescence with an emission maximum at 550 nm, a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 32.4%, and substantially mitigated efficiency roll-off relative to conventional cis-quinacridone emitters. This work establishes orbital-symmetry engineering as a rational strategy for decoupling orbital symmetry from overall molecular symmetry, providing a general approach to transforming intrinsically weak luminophores into efficient narrowband emitters.

item.title: Nano Letters: A Skin-like Hydrogel with Multidimensional Fillers for Stable Human–Machine Interaction
item.description:
Shengxin Xiang, Lei Liu, Xiao Wei, Feixiang Gao, Yu Lin, Zhiwei Zhao, Xinkai Xie, Jun Wu
The deep integration of human–machine interface (HMI) technology and the Internet of Things (IoT) has imposed stringent new requirements for electronic skin (e-skin) in terms of flexibility, comfort, and high sensitivity. Herein we present a multiconductive network hydrogel e-skin (MCNHE-skin) based on a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) dual-network matrix with polydopamine (PDA), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and MXene as conductive fillers. The MCNHE-skin exhibits electrical conductivity (<5 kΩ), high stretchability (∼650%), strong self-adhesion (∼19 kPa), and low modulus (∼3.6 kPa). These characteristics enable its successful application in multimodal sensing systems such as strain sensors, pressure sensors, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), and physiological signal monitors. Furthermore, by integration with flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs), MCNHE-skin is developed into smart wearable systems for noncontact HMI. The 0D/1D/2D synergistic conductive network presented in this hydrogel e-skin yields high-fidelity sensing and noncontact control capabilities, marking a significant step forward in the development of multifunctional wearable electronics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Targeting the Immune-Neurovascular Interface to Ameliorate Pericyte Dysfunction with a Multifunctional Peptide–Drug Conjugate Nanoprodrug for Multiple Sclerosis Therapy
item.description:
Yongkang Mu, Kaichao Wen, Lingling Zhou, Zhiyong Gu, Tianying Wang, Yixian Li, Xiyu Yang, Xuan Liu, et al.
Pericyte dysfunction triggers blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption and subsequent aberrant immune infiltration in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet targeted interventions remain lacking. Here, we engineered a dual-functional fusion peptide (VLC) for pericyte targeting and therapeutic intervention and subsequently conjugated it with luteolin to construct a peptide–drug conjugate (PDC)-based ROS-responsive nanoprodrug (VLC@Lut-NPs). This system significantly suppressed MMP-9 overactivation and mitigated neuroinflammation. To optimize the pharmacokinetic profile of the PDC nanotherapeutic, we adopted subcutaneous administration, achieving a prolonged circulation half-life and enhancing brain drug accumulation (AUCbrain) by 2.65-fold compared with intravenous injection. In two MS models, VLC@Lut-NPs restored pericyte homeostasis, reinforced BBB integrity, attenuated aberrant peripheral immune infiltration, and ultimately promoted myelin repair and regeneration. Notably, a once-every-other-day subcutaneous regimen outperformed daily intravenous administration. By bridging peripheral immunity and the neurovascular unit, this work identifies pericytes as a central regulatory node and establishes a pericyte-targeted PDC nanoplatform for durable MS treatment, highlighting its translational potential as a complementary strategy to conventional immunomodulatory approaches.

item.title: ACS Nano: Generation of Bloch Points with Controlled Spin Texture Using Geometrical Boundary Conditions
item.description:
Naëmi Leo, Daniel Wolf, Alicia Estela Herguedas-Alonso, Oleksandr Zaiets, Jakub Jurczyk, Takeaki Gokita, John Fullerton, Dedalo Sanz-Hernandez, et al.
Bloch points are three-dimensional topological singularities in magnetization that play a key role in topological transformations of spin textures such as skyrmion creation or annihilation. While topology often enforces the existence of Bloch points in confined geometries such as cylindrical nanowires, deterministic control over their position and magnetic configuration remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the generation of Bloch points with controlled spin texture by engineering geometrical boundary conditions in three-dimensional nanomagnets. By introducing a chirality interface between two three-dimensional double-helix nanowires of opposite handedness, forming a kinked, noncollinear structure, we impose competing topological constraints that uniquely define the magnetization configuration surrounding the Bloch point. A saturating magnetic field nucleates head-to-head or tail-to-tail domain configurations at the chirality interface, producing a Bloch-point domain wall with deterministic polarity, circulation, and helicity. This geometrical approach enables full three-dimensional control of Bloch point domain walls, allowing deterministic engineering of their spin texture and its selective coupling to current-induced Oersted fields.

item.title: JACS: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
item.description:
Yan-Xuan Wu, Jia-Heng Hu, Yuan Xu, Pu-Fan Qian, Ke-Xin Kong, Qi-Jun Yao, Tao Zhou, Bing-Feng Shi
The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

item.title: ACS Nano: Flexible Zwitterionic Hydrogel Ultrasonic Patch Enables Spatiotemporally Controlled Delivery of Mangiferin-Loaded Micelles for Accelerating Diabetic Wound Healing
item.description:
Danyang Chen, Qiao Li, Xiawei Zhao, Hongying Wang, Qiuli Wu, Haolun Wang, Hao Zhong, Mi Zhou, et al.
Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired angiogenesis, and delayed tissue remodeling, often resulting in chronic nonhealing ulcers. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) offers a promising noninvasive therapeutic strategy; however, its clinical efficacy remains constrained by unstable acoustic coupling interfaces and the lack of integrated biological activity. Here, we report an ultrasound-responsive zwitterionic hydrogel patch by incorporating mangiferin-loaded micelles into a topologically entangled PCBOH hydrogel (MF@PCBOH). The mechanically robust hydrogel forms a stable and conformal acoustic interface that efficiently transmits ultrasound under dynamic conditions, whereas the incorporated micelles improve the aqueous dispersibility of mangiferin and enable ultrasound-enhanced release. Under LIPUS stimulation, released mangiferin reduces intracellular ROS, shifts macrophages toward a reparative phenotype, promotes endothelial angiogenesis, and enhances cell migration. As a result, MF@PCBOH accelerates diabetic wound healing in rats, accompanied by reduced inflammation, improved collagen remodeling, and enhanced vascular maturation. Similar therapeutic benefits are observed in a full-thickness porcine wound model, supporting the effectiveness of the hydrogel patch in a large-animal setting. This study demonstrates that integrating a durable acoustic interface with ultrasound-responsive drug delivery offers an effective strategy for diabetic wound repair.

item.title: JACS: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
item.description:
Chen Gong, Jialu Chen, Haopeng Wang, Liwei Tang, Jingtian Zhang, Yi Liu, Junhua Luo, Zhihua Sun
Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Boosting Electron/Mass Transport via Interfacial Coupling in a Dual-Supported Catalyst toward Ampere-Level Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
Peng Wang, Meijun Liu, Tiantian Ma, Tong Sun, Weixuan An, Fengkai Liu, Nian Ran, Jianjun Liu, et al.
Developing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts with high activity and long-term durability at industrial current densities remains challenging because catalytic kinetics, electron transport, and mass transport must be optimized simultaneously. Here, we report a one-pot method to anchor Pt-single-atom-modified NiCoP onto MXene with a high surface coverage of ∼97%. The Pt-NiCoP@MXene catalyst requires overpotentials of only 13.8 and 175 mV in 1 M KOH to deliver 10 and 1000 mA cm–2, respectively, and exhibits an ultralow decay rate of 7.1 μV h–1 over 1000 h at 1000 mA cm–2 in a three-electrode system. In an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer, it achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.74 V in a 4 cm2 cell with 98% voltage retention after 1000 h and maintains 97% retention over 500 h with a scaled 25 cm2 cell. Experiments and DFT calculations demonstrate the interface strong coupling via Ni/Co–O–Ti bonding bridges NiCoP and MXene effectively and accelerates the electron transport of catalytic layer, while the uniform dispersion of NiCoP on MXene improves surface wettability and facilitates bubble release and electrolyte replenishment. Additionally, Pt–P coordination increases the metallicity of Pt atoms and optimizes hydrogen adsorption/desorption. This work provides a facile strategy for synthesizing high-quality dual-supported catalysts and validates their industrial application potential.

item.title: JACS: Macrocycle Screening against the C-Terminal Region of CHD4 Uncovers Its Role as an Interaction Hub in the Formation of the Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase Complex
item.description:
David C. Williams, Jie Ren, Torry Li, Jarrett M. Pelton, Dhanushi Dedakia, Brandon Novy, Konstantin I. Popov, Robert K. McGinty, et al.
The Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase complex (NuRD) plays a key role in regulating hemoglobin expression in adult erythroid cells. Selectively disrupting this complex potently induces the expression of fetal hemoglobin, a proven therapeutic strategy for treating beta-hemoglobinopathies such as sickle cell anemia. In these studies, we have used mRNA display to identify small macrocyclic peptides that inhibit the interaction between two core components of NuRD, the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 and the CR2 domain of GATAD2A. In addition, the screen suggested a second binding site on the CHD4 domain. Based on this observation, we hypothesized and confirmed that CDK2AP1 bound to this region of CHD4, leading us to purify and determine the structure of the ternary complex between CHD4, GATAD2A, and CDK2AP1. The results of our studies show that the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 functions as a critical interaction hub in the formation of NuRD and suggest a strategy to block NuRD function for therapy.

item.title: JACS: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
item.description:
Yanming Zhao, Xikai Chen, Changgui Lv, Yu Yan, Jinyu Liu, Yassin H. Andaloussi, Michael J. Zaworotko, Yun-Lei Peng
Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

item.title: JACS: Artificial Light-Harvesting Nanotubes: Intermolecular Charge Transfer beyond the Exciton Model
item.description:
Davide Giavazzi, Anna Painelli
Self-assembled nanotubes of C8S3 cyanine dyes have been widely investigated as model systems for light-harvesting complexes. Recently published data point to a brick-layer molecular arrangement in the nanotubes, in contrast to the herringbone structure previously adopted to explain the absorption and linear dichroism data within the exciton model. Here we solve this conundrum by showing that, relying on the brick-layer structure as extracted from cryo-EM, the exciton model can properly account for the observed spectral features, provided it is extended to account for intermolecular charge-transfer interactions.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanoscale Spintronic Microwave Devices: From Fundamental Mechanisms to Emerging Applications
item.description:
Shuhui Liu, Bin Fang, Yawen Luo, Like Zhang, Zhenhao Liu, Dongxing Zheng, Yan Zhou, Giovanni Finocchio, et al.
With the rapid deployment of next-generation communication technologies, the demand for highly sensitive and miniaturized microwave detectors has become extremely urgent. Conventional semiconductor diodes suffer from intrinsic drawbacks when detecting submicrowatt signals. Spintronics provides an optimal alternative via the spin rectification effect, which enables widely tunable, low-power microwave rectification at room temperature. This Review examines recent advances in spintronic microwave rectifiers and their future prospects. We discuss diverse physical platforms, including devices with uniform magnetization and special nonuniform topological spin textures. Furthermore, we highlight multiorder-of-magnitude performance improvements in such devices, focusing on strategies to boost sensitivity, reduce noise equivalent power (NEP), and extend broadband as well as multiband detection capacity. Apart from core performance metrics, we discuss emerging applications: ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting, high-resolution vector microwave-field imaging, monolithically integrated spintronic microwave systems, and microwave neural networks that can directly process high-frequency signals for neuromorphic computing. By sorting out the complete technical development route of this field, this Review aims to provide a systematic theoretical framework and technical references to promote the development of spintronic devices for next-generation wireless communication and edge artificial intelligence.

item.title: ACS Nano: Emergent Phenomena in Wurtzite Ferroelectric Semiconductors
item.description:
Haoze Zhang, Alexei Gruverman, Pankaj Sharma
The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.

item.title: JACS: Integrated Solid/Solution NMR Assignment Enables Mapping of Dynamics and Ligand Binding in a 134 kDa Enzyme
item.description:
Federico Napoli, Rajkumar Singh, Anna Kapitonova, Virgil Aitenbichler, Giorgia Toscano, Barbara Perrone, Paul Schanda
Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Here, we present an integrated magic-angle spinning (MAS) and solution NMR study of the 134 kDa tetrameric malate dehydrogenase from Ignicoccus islandicus (IiMDH), an enzyme of particular interest as an evolutionary intermediate between allosteric lactate dehydrogenases and nonallosteric malate dehydrogenases. By combining high-dimensional (up to 4D) MAS NMR experiments on sedimented protein with solution NMR, we achieved 92% backbone heavy-atom assignment and 91% assignment of all Ile-δ1, Leu-δ1/-δ2, Val-γ1/-γ2, Met-ε, and Thr-γ methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues. The integrated approach demonstrated here exploits the distinct strengths of MAS and solution NMR and provides a comprehensive view of structure, dynamics, and substrate interactions in a large oligomeric enzyme that neither technique could provide alone.

item.title: JACS: Probing the Conformational Behavior of a Seven Hetero-Spin Supramolecule
item.description:
Lubomir Loci, Tom S. Bennett, Selena J. Lockyer, George F. S. Whitehead, Grigore A. Timco, Giulia Da Ros, Ciarán J. Rogers, Adam Brookfield, et al.
The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable. Orientation-selective Double Electron Electron Resonance (DEER) and Relaxation Induced Dipolar Modulation Enhancement (RIDME) spectroscopies are used to selectively probe the different spin-spin interactions in the frozen solution phase and to define differences from the solid-state crystal structure.

item.title: JACS: Encapsulation-Activated Deep-NIR Triarylmethane Dyes via Steric Hindrance Engineering for Long-Circulating Fluorescence/Photoacoustic Dual-Modal Bioimaging
item.description:
Xiaodong Zhang, Hui Bian, Yangting Qiu, Ruwei Wei, Youjun Yang, Bo Tang
NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. It offers a general and well-defined paradigm for high-fidelity deep-tissue imaging and provides a promising strategy for further development of precision diagnostics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Turn Shield into Sword: Pathological Hydroxyapatite-Targeting Micelles Drive Metabolic Stress-Induced Autophagy Dysfunction for Bone Metastasis Therapy
item.description:
Yunxia Ye, Ruilin Wang, Shipei Nie, Tongxin Liu, Tingchen Tian, Ziyan Dong, Dong Chen, Ling Ma, et al.
Bone metastasis remains a major clinical challenge in advanced breast cancer because therapeutic efficacy is limited by poor lesion targeting and systemic toxicity. Moreover, the hypoxic bone microenvironment induces protective autophagy in tumor cells, which maintains metabolic homeostasis and limits therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we develop a bone metastasis-targeted micellar system (AD/R) to overcome this protective autophagy “shield”. Based on the low crystallinity of pathological hydroxyapatite (HAP) and the hypoxic bone microenvironment, a pathological HAP-targeting polymer (DSPE-PEG-ALN, DPA) and a hypoxia-responsive polymer (DSPE-AZO-PEG, DAP) are coassembled into micelles encapsulating the oxidative phosphorylation inhibitor resveratrol (RES). Following selective accumulation in bone-metastatic lesions, AD/R undergoes hypoxia-triggered disassembly. The released DPA induces calcium-mediated membrane mineralization to restrict oxygen and nutrient supply, whereas RES suppresses oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production. This “external blockade” and “internal disruption” synergistically aggravate metabolic stress, activate AMPK-dependent autophagy, and impair lysosomal degradation through lysosomal membrane permeabilization, ultimately inducing autophagy dysfunction and autophagy-associated tumor cell death. In murine breast cancer bone metastasis models, AD/R effectively suppresses bone and secondary lung metastases and restores bone homeostasis. This work establishes a “turn shield into sword” paradigm by converting protective autophagy into metabolic stress-induced autophagy dysfunction for the treatment of bone metastasis.

item.title: Nano Letters: Dielectric Interfaces Reshape Dynamic Single-Molecule Optical Fingerprints in Nanometer-Thick Polymer Films
item.description:
Daniel Marx, David Malsbenden, Ivan Gligonov, Dominik Wöll, Jörg Enderlein, Oleksii Nevskyi
Fluorescence lifetimes near dielectric interfaces depend on molecular dipole orientation, but this relationship becomes more complex when emitters are confined within finite nanometer-thick polymer films. Here, we combine radially polarized excitation imaging with time-correlated single-photon counting to follow the orientation and fluorescence lifetime of individual PDI molecules undergoing rotational motion in thin poly(n-butyl methacrylate) films. Orientation-sensitive fluorescence patterns were analyzed using vectorial wave-optical simulations, enabling dipole orientation and excited-state lifetime to be correlated over time for the same emitter. The lifetime–orientation relationships vary systematically with film thickness and between molecules within the same film. Electrodynamic calculations for the glass–polymer–air geometry reproduce the principal trends and show that the observed heterogeneity is consistent with different axial emitter positions. These results establish single molecular dipoles as probes of finite nanometer-thick dielectric environments.

item.title: JACS: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
item.description:
Yuang Cui, Yizhou Chen, Hui Lv, Rao Liang, Beibei Zhan, Xiaheng Zhang
The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

item.title: JACS: Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
item.description:
Wei Zeng, Chong-An Chen, Congcong Jin, Jiachen Lu, Chanhee Ko, Sooyeon Lee, Taek Rim Kim, Se Chan Noh, et al.
Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.

item.title: Nano Letters: Erbium Probes of Magnetic Order in a van der Waals Material
item.description:
Guadalupe García-Arellano, Gabriel I. López-Morales, Kang Xu, Samra Husremović, Jiayi Li, Arun Ramanathan, Xavier Roy, Cyrus E. Dreyer, et al.
Embedded atomic emitters offer a complementary approach to characterizing magnetism in two-dimensional materials by accessing the magnetic environment from within. Here, we demonstrate that ion-implanted Er3+ centers act as internal optical probes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. Temperature-dependent telecom photoluminescence reveals signatures of the magnetic transition, persistent local magnetic behavior above the bulk Néel temperature, pronounced thermal hysteresis, and redistribution of optical spectral weight near the transition. Upon cooling, the Er resonances sharpen to the instrumental limit, pointing to remarkably homogeneous local environments despite implantation. Measurements spanning a 20-fold range of implantation fluence, structural characterization, and first-principles calculations suggest that the detected emission originates predominantly from an optically active subset of Er centers occupying well-defined environments and minimally perturbing the host magnetism. These results establish rare-earth defects as embedded probes of local magnetism and open opportunities for quantum-optical interrogation at individual lattice sites.

item.title: JACS: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
item.description:
Pengzhan Wang, Peihua Lin, Bo Zhang, Dushuo Feng, Qiyue Wang, Pan Tao, Hui Du, Fangyuan Li, et al.
Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.

item.title: JACS: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
item.description:
Haruka Kano, Takashi Harimoto, Yasutomo Segawa
Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

item.title: Nano Letters: Photobattery Architectures to Suppress Charge Recombination
item.description:
Kohei Shimokawa, Byung-Man Kim, Arvind Pujari, Hooman Abbasi, Tetsu Ichitsubo, Michael De Volder
Integrating solar energy conversion and storage into single-unit photobatteries offers compact energy supplies. However, achieving sufficient photovoltage to charge batteries without external bias remains a critical bottleneck for these devices. Here, we demonstrate that the photovoltage in Zn-ion photobatteries can be modulated and enhanced by selecting and structuring the photoactive materials strategically. Randomly dispersed electrode configurations are easy to manufacture but they can suffer from charge recombination. In our experiments, these yielded a negligible photovoltage of ∼0.01 V. In comparison, our proposed layer-by-layer design, integrating a solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) with an optimized spinel Zn–Mn oxide cathode, increased the photovoltage output to ∼1 V under 1-sun illumination. This dramatic performance enhancement is achieved by better control over interfaces and charge transport and establishes a strategy for improving the architecture of future photobatteries.

item.title: ACS Nano: Robust and Wide-Range Friction Regulation via Interfacial Bridging-Promoted Hydration Switching in Phase-Separated Gels
item.description:
Yunsong Kong, Bingbing Liu, Yunlei Zhang, Weiyi Zhao, Luyao Gao, Xiaoduo Zhao, Yong-min Liang, Shuanhong Ma, et al.
Interfacial friction strongly influences materials performance, but achieving controllable friction with both high robustness and wide-range tunability remains difficult. In conventional friction regulation systems based on phase separations, rigid and incompatible hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces often cause interfacial cracking and poor stability. Here, inspired by the toughening mechanism of cartilage, we introduce amphiphilic bridging segments between hydrophilic and hydrophobic phases to construct an interfacial bridging nanophase-separated gel (IBNSGel) for robust friction control. This design transforms the fragile phase interface into a tough bridging interphase, suppresses aggregation, promotes uniform nanophase separation, and enhances interfacial stability during hydration-induced phase separation. Owing to this bridging effect, IBNSGel exhibits synergistic surface-bulk friction switching upon hydration: the surface forms a stable hydration layer for excellent lubrication, while the bulk hardens with higher modulus and lower damping, reducing conformal contact dissipation. As a result, this gel achieves stable, reversible, and wide-range coefficient of friction (CoF) switching during hydration–dehydration, with switching ratios of 150 at the macroscale and 330 at the microscale. Based on its excellent multimedium stability and biocompatibility, this friction control material demonstrates great application potential in smart medical devices, soft robots, and interface intelligent transportation systems.

item.title: ACS Nano: Unconventionally Dynamical Regime of Colloidal Nanocrystals on Spherical Surfaces
item.description:
Yuming Wang, Xiaobin Dai, Yibo Wu, Lijuan Gao, Wenlong Chen, Linghe Cheng, Xueqing Jin, Li-Tang Yan
Crystallography of colloidal nanocrystals on spherical surfaces underpins the structural organization of a wide range of functional soft and biological materials, from viral capsids and protein nanocages to colloidal microcapsules and curvature-engineered metamaterials. In these systems, the topology dictates that crystalline order on a sphere must incorporate topological defects that can self-organize into scars whose conformations undergo fluctuations. However, how these conformations collectively affect phase transitions on spheres remains unknown. Here, we investigate the phase transitions of colloidal nanocrystal packing on the spherical surface and identify an unconventional regime in the solid phase, which exhibits rapid dynamics with enhanced fluctuations of scars. Further analysis reveals that this regime is governed by the conformational entropy of the scars. Such an entropic effect on dynamics exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on system size and causes disparate scaling laws at intermediate and large system sizes, which are absent in previous experiments and theoretical models. The findings provide insights into the effect of topological defects on curved manifolds and reveal the critical role of the conformational entropy of defect scars in geometrically frustrated systems of colloidal nanocrystals.

item.title: JACS: Entropy-Driven Dynamic Oxygen Cycling on High-Entropy Oxides Enables Coke-Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane
item.description:
Zhenpeng Wang, Tian Qin, Jing Xiong, Yitao Yang, Dawei Han, Xuanzhen Li, Hao Guo, Chenxi Yang, et al.
Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.

item.title: JACS: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
item.description:
Souvick Biswas, Sabrina Arias, Shane J. Goettl, Nureshan Dias, Stanislaw F. Wnuk, Musahid Ahmed, Alexander M. Mebel, Ralf I. Kaiser
Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.

item.title: ACS Nano: Electronic Structure Modulation in Isomeric Carborane-Thiolated Cu4 Nanoclusters Boosts CO2 Electroreduction to Methane
item.description:
Juhina Nisar, Arijit Jana, Zhengyuan Li, Harpriya Minhas, Astrid Campos Mata, Jithu Raj, Yu-Cheng Liu, Tomas Base, et al.
Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) to energy-dense hydrocarbons is central to sustainable carbon recycling, although achieving selective conversion at high current density and lower overpotential remains challenging. Here, we explore three molecularly precise nanomaterials, comprising nearly square planar Cu4 kernel protected by isomeric carborane-thiolate (CBT) cages, viz., Cu4-oCBT (ortho-carborane), Cu4-mCBT (meta-carborane), and Cu4-ICBT (iodinated-ortho-carborane), for eCO2R. Among them, Cu4-mCBT shows the most favorable performance, achieving ∼74% overall eCO2R selectivity and a CH4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of ∼45% at high current densities of 500 mA cm–2 (−0.87 V vs RHE) while maintaining promising production of C2+ products. Furthermore, Cu4-mCBT and Cu4-ICBT catalysts deliver industrially relevant CH4 partial current densities (JCH4 ∼ 323 mA cm–2 at −0.99 V) at low overpotential, representing competitive performance compared to Cu nanoclusters (NCs) stabilized by conventional ligands. First-principles calculations reveal that Cu4-mCBT lowers the free energy barrier for *CHO to *CHOH hydrogenation, the rate-limiting step for methane formation, due to better orbital interactions with the intermediates. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) confirms the transient intermediate species formed in the predicted eCO2R-to-CH4 pathway. Charge density difference, projected density of states, and in situ X-ray absorption studies demonstrate the primary catalytic role of the Cu-core, while three-dimensional cage-like ligand shells modulate the electronic structure of exposed metal atoms, thereby optimizing the intermediate binding. This study investigates the catalytic performance of carborane-appended tetranuclear copper clusters toward CO2 reduction pathways and elucidates their structure–activity relationships.

item.title: JACS: Substrate Length Controls Atropopeptide Complexity and Triggers Excision-Driven Scaffold Hop to Diketopiperazine Alkaloids
item.description:
Bin Tan, Ziheng Cui, Yuya Kakumu, Sandra J. Panczyk, Mai Ikeda, Dongyu Liu, Christine M. Pestalozzi, Julia A. Vorholt, et al.
Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.

item.title: Nano Letters: Directional Manufacturing of Defect Mitigation and Large-Scale Single-Crystalline Metal Foils via Gas Flow Optimization toward Commercialization
item.description:
The-Hung Mai, Thi H. Ho, Shi-Hui Liu, Santhoshkumar S, Muhammad Adnan, Arvind Chandrasekar, Tuan V. Vu, Chien-Cheng Kuo, et al.
Single-crystalline metals, with their distinctive symmetries, are the ideal medium for high-order molecular arrangement and the diminishing of grain boundaries and defect sites coupled with high anisotropy. However, conventional synthesis via bulk growth or epitaxial deposition remains complex, costly, and difficult to scale. Here, we report a simple and inexpensive strategy as an alternative to conventional strategies for manufacturing single-crystalline metal foils. Miraculously, by miniaturization of grain boundaries and promoting surface energy minimization during the rotation of the crystal lattice followed by the consumption of neighboring grains, high-quality and large-scale single-crystalline metal foils (Cu(111), Ni(111)) were obtained via vertically suspended chemical vapor deposition (CVD) annealing of polycrystalline metal foils. This discovery offers a potential strategy for manipulating and producing large-scale metal foils that may be used for industrial-scale applications.

item.title: ACS Nano: A Capacitively Coupled Dual-Gate 2D Transistor Unifying Logic-in-Memory and Tunable Synaptic Plasticity
item.description:
Min He, Gaochen Yang, Bo Jiang, Xiaohan Meng, Xiao He, Langlang Xu, Shengjie Lv, Guanting Liu, et al.
Integrating logic control with adaptive synaptic learning at the device level is a key step toward high-performance computing-in-memory (CIM) hardware. However, the integration of logic-in-memory (LIM) and synaptic plasticity within a homogeneous device is hindered by the incompatibility between stable logic output and dynamic weight modulation. Here, we demonstrate a logic-synapse function-integrated device based on a two-dimensional (2D) floating-gate field-effect transistor (FGFET) with a coplanar dual-control-gate architecture. With two independent gate-coupling coefficients, the nominally symmetric design allows the gate-induced potential increments to superpose on the floating gate: cooperative inputs induce charge tunneling and write a new memory state, whereas antagonistic inputs approximately cancel the pulse-induced potential increment and latch the stored state. This rule directly implements LIM within a single device, enabling 14 reconfigurable Boolean logic operations with in situ nonvolatile output storage, a logic read margin of 104, and no external cascading for the demonstrated two-input logic functions. The same coupling framework further supports tunable synaptic plasticity, including lateral enhancement/inhibition and spatiotemporal competition/cooperation among multiple synaptic inputs. In particular, asynchronous competitive modulation modifies history-dependent conductance updates, improving the depression nonlinearity to 0.0833 while retaining a dynamic range of 22.82. These results establish an all-electrical device-level route for integrating logic control and neural weight adaptation in compact CIM hardware.

item.title: JACS: Light Ignites Lattice Oxygen in an Asymmetric Motif
item.description:
Jiali Wang, Fanghua Zeng, Rui Xiong, Shuangqing Liu, Zhiqi Wen, Ziyue Cheng, Cejun Hu, Baisheng Sa, et al.
Lattice-oxygen-mediated pathways bypass the energy-intensive steps that constrain adsorbate-mediated catalysis. Activating these pathways under mild conditions, however, means breaking metal–oxygen bonds that are, by design, strong. Asymmetric M1-O-M2 motifs, in which a bridging oxygen sits between two cations of different electronic character, decouple oxygen activation from oxygen release by distributing these functions across chemically distinct sites. Here, we show that a Cu-doped In2O3 system with a well-defined asymmetric Cu–O–In unit exhibits enhanced photoinduced lattice oxygen activity. Series (quasi) in situ spectroscopy captures the activation, consumption, and replenishment of lattice oxygen under illumination in real time. Photogenerated carriers populate around the Cu–O site preferentially, weakening the Cu–O bond enough to extract lattice oxygen at room temperature. The optimized material, Cui-In2O3, gives a response of 32.4 toward 5 ppm of H2S under visible light. The results connect local coordination asymmetry directly to photoinduced oxygen functionality and suggest a route toward photodriven catalysts built around asymmetric oxygen sites.

item.title: JACS: Leveraging Cubenes to Access Highly Functionalized Fused Cubes
item.description:
Sarah A. French, Christina A. Rivera, Kasey K. Chung, K. N. Houk, Neil K. Garg
Since 1913, cubane has fascinated chemists owing to its remarkable structure. More recently, however, cubanes have emerged as attractive bioisosteres for aromatic rings. Although substituted derivatives are relatively common, ring-fused cubanes (a.k.a. “fused cubes”) are rare and can be difficult to access. Here, we report a strategy for the synthesis of fused cubes leveraging cubenes, unusual fleeting intermediates possessing hyperpyramidalized alkenes, in strain-promoted trapping reactions. Further, experimental and computational studies for the generation and reactivity of unsubstituted cubene and new substituted cubenes are disclosed. These studies not only push the limits of strained intermediate chemistry but also provide an entryway to highly functionalized fused cubes, including new three-dimensional hybrid structures and other unprecedented chemical space.

item.title: JACS: Simulating Chemical Reaction Dynamics Using Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization: A Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Approach
item.description:
Sumit Kumar, Kalpak Ghosh, Deepak Kumar, Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
Quantum computers offer the potential to simulate chemical systems beyond the capabilities of classical computers. However, current quantum computing approaches to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and vibrational analysis largely rely on the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), whose circuit depth, iterative optimization, and measurement overhead hinder the practical simulation of molecular systems. Here, we extend Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), a quantum sampling-based electronic-structure method, to AIMD and vibrational analysis on noisy quantum hardware. The resulting framework enables nuclear forces and Hessians to be derived from quantum-computed electronic energies, facilitating molecular dynamics and characterization of potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate the approach using diverse molecular processes, including H2 bond vibration, the proton-exchange reaction (H+ + H2), the bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction (Cl– + CH3Cl), and proton-transfer dynamics between two water molecules involving transient formation of the Zundel cation (H2O···H+···OH2). Across these systems, SQD-AIMD trajectories and vibrational frequencies obtained with noisy quantum hardware/noise-models show excellent agreement with classical reference calculations and substantially improved accuracy relative to previously reported VQE-based simulations. Importantly, the SQD-based approach eliminates costly variational optimization and significantly reduces measurement requirements relative to VQE, enabling AIMD simulations spanning approximately 500 timesteps (∼200 fs), substantially longer than previously reported AIMD simulations on quantum hardware.
